tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: propose it and call this.

The result says which case below applies. When the box shows your question, it ends your turn: write no text after this call, since the recap and question say what the user needs and your work above holds the detail. Otherwise your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, with any question the box did not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead, an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence; the detail goes in message. No "@", no leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

message.description: For a reply: what the click sends, up to 300 characters of plain text — no "@" anywhere, no leading / or !. Omit when the label is the whole message.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

# Gondola Royale: Game Spec & Hackathon Plan

Oct 16, 2026 · @Mex

## The pitch

Gondola Royale (working title) is a party deathmatch for 4 to 18 people
in one room. Teams crew armed gondolas in a 3D Venice shown on one big
screen, and their phones are the controllers. One hit sinks a boat, a
sunk boat is back in 5 seconds, and after 5 minutes the team with the
most kills wins.

The core loop, in one 5-minute match:

1.  Each team spawns at a random dock with empty hands.

2.  Teams race to floating crates for weapons and powers, like the

    so the looting never stops.

3.  Teams hunt in the wide canals or ambush from the narrow side canals.

4.  One hit sinks a boat. The shooter's team scores a kill; the sunk
    team takes a death.

5.  Five seconds later the sunk boat respawns at a random dock with
    nothing. At 5:00 the team with the most kills wins.

- **Nobody is a passenger.** Every role has something to do every

# Gondola Royale: Game Spec & Hackathon Plan

Oct 16, 2026 · @Mex

## The pitch

Gondola Royale (working title) is a party deathmatch for 4 to 18 people
in one room. Teams crew armed gondolas in a 3D Venice shown on one big
screen, and their phones are the controllers. One hit sinks a boat, a
sunk boat is back in 5 seconds, and after 5 minutes the team with the
most kills wins.

The core loop, in one 5-minute match:

1.  Each team spawns at a random dock with empty hands.

2.  Teams race to floating crates for weapons and powers, like the
    pickups in Blur. Every weapon has only a few shots (5 by default),
    so the looting never stops.

3.  Teams hunt in the wide canals or ambush from the narrow side canals.

4.  One hit sinks a boat. The shooter's team scores a kill; the sunk
    team takes a death.

5.  Five seconds later the sunk boat respawns at a random dock with
    nothing. At 5:00 the team with the most kills wins.

Design rules we hold ourselves to:

- **Nobody is a passenger.** Every role has something to do every
  second.

- **The big screen tells the story.** Anyone in the room can follow who
  is winning at a glance.

- **Zero friction.** Scan, tap, play in under 30 seconds. No install, no
  account.

- **Death is short, never final.** A sunk crew is back in 5 seconds, so
  nobody stands around watching.

What changes from the Regata Storica concept: racing is gone. We keep
phones as controllers, the big screen, QR join and the HTTPS
motion-sensor lesson. The Doge in VR and the printed trophy move to
stretch goals.

## 1. Platform rules

One web app, one URL, two modes. Nothing gets installed anywhere.

| Mode | Runs on | Does | Never does |
|----|----|----|----|
| SCENE | The PC wired to the projector, opened once | Runs the whole game: simulation, physics, 3D rendering, split screen, audio. It is the single source of truth. | Read phone sensors |
| PLAYER | Every phone | Reads touch and motion sensors, sends inputs, shows a control pad plus status (role, ammo, team score, respawn countdown) | Render the game world or any 3D |
| Relay server | A small Node process | Routes messages between phones and the scene by room code | Game logic of any kind |

Hard requirements:

- **HTTPS everywhere.** iOS only grants motion sensors and the camera on
  secure pages, and only after a user tap.

- **Browsers:** Safari on iOS 16+ and Chrome on Android for phones.
  Chrome on the scene PC.

- **Phone orientation:** landscape for Pilot and Gunner. Show a "rotate
  your phone" overlay otherwise, since iOS ignores orientation lock.

- **Scene PC:** a laptop or PC with a dedicated GPU, 1080p output to the
  projector.

- **Keyboard fallback:** every role can be played from the scene PC
  keyboard. This is both the dev test harness and the backup if a phone
  fails mid-demo.

## 2. Joining, teams and the split screen

Players join by scanning a QR with the phone's normal camera, which
drops them straight into the lobby. One change from the original idea:
the QR carries the room link, so phones don't need an in-app scanner.

1.  On the projector PC, open the app and pick **SCENE**. It creates a
    room with a 4-letter code (for example RIVA) and shows a large QR,
    the code and a short URL.

2.  Players scan the QR with the phone camera. The QR encodes
    https://\<host\>/play?room=RIVA, so the phone opens directly in
    PLAYER mode inside that room.

    - The **PLAYER** button on the landing page stays as a fallback. It
      opens an in-app QR scanner plus a field to type the 4-letter code.

    - Why the change: an in-app scanner adds a camera permission prompt
      and a library. The native camera skips both.

3.  The phone shows a random Venetian nickname (editable) and one big
    **Enable controls** button. That single tap is required: it triggers
    the iOS motion permission and the screen wake lock.

4.  The player appears on the big screen, slotted into a team and a
    role.

5.  The host starts the round from the scene PC (Start button or Space
    bar).

**Team assignment**

- The host picks team size in the lobby: 3 (default) or 2. Twelve people
  in teams of 3 gives 4 teams and a clean 2×2 screen.

- Players fill teams in join order. Inside a team, roles fill in order:
  Pilot, then Gunner, then Engineer.

- Until the round starts, a player can swap role with a teammate or move
  to any team with a free slot, from the phone.

- Maximum 6 teams, because that is the most viewports a projector can
  show readably.

- Odd counts are balanced, not left over: 7 players in teams of 3
  becomes 3 + 2 + 2, never 3 + 3 + 1.

Short-handed teams merge roles automatically:

| Members | Who does what |
|----|----|
| 3 | Pilot, Gunner, Engineer |
| 2 | Pilot. The Gunner also gets the two power buttons. Bailing water happens automatically at half speed. |
| 1 (stretch) | Solo controller: tilt to steer with auto-throttle, one FIRE button that auto-targets the nearest enemy ahead |

**Split-screen layouts** on a 16:9 screen, fixed for the whole round so
people don't lose track of their view:

| Teams | Layout                  | Spare cell                              |
|-------|-------------------------|-----------------------------------------|
| 2     | Two side-by-side halves | None                                    |
| 3     | 2×2 grid                | Live overview map                       |
| 4     | 2×2 grid                | None, minimap sits where the cells meet |
| 5     | 3×2 grid                | Live overview map                       |
| 6     | 3×2 grid                | None, minimap sits where the cells meet |

Each viewport has a thick border in the team colour and the team name.
Team colours: Rosso, Azzurro, Verde, Oro, Viola, Arancio. When a boat
sinks, its cell shows a 5 s kill-cam on the boat that sank it, with a
countdown, then cuts back to the respawned boat.

## 3. Roles and phone controls

One boat per team, one job per player. The third role (Engineer) is our
addition so teams of 3 have a real job, not a spectator seat.

### Pilot: drives the boat

On screen: the gondolier standing at the stern with the oar.

- Hold the phone in landscape with both hands, like a steering wheel.
  Rotate it left or right to steer. Dead zone of 4°, full lock at 35°.

- Right thumb holds **GAS** (the whole right half of the screen). Left
  thumb holds **BRAKE / REVERSE** (the left half).

- Hold BRAKE while steering at speed for a **drift turn**: sharper turn,
  loses speed.

- **Ramming:** hitting an enemy at high speed while boosted sinks them.
  This gives the Pilot an attack of their own.

- **Calibration:** during the countdown the Pilot holds the phone in a
  comfortable position and taps CALIBRATE. That angle becomes
  "straight".

- Phone shows a big steering-wheel graphic that rotates live with the
  tilt. This feedback is essential, since the Pilot is looking at the
  wall, not the phone.

### Gunner: aims with the gyroscope and shoots

On screen: seated mid-boat behind a swivel cannon that turns with the
aim.

- Hold the phone in landscape with both hands, like a camera, and turn
  it left or right to turn the view and the cannon. **Gyroscope only:**
  no dragging, no looking up or down. Full rules in section 4.

- **FIRE:** the whole right two-thirds of the screen is one big button.
  Tap to fire, hold for auto-fire where the weapon allows it.

- **RECENTER:** a smaller button on the left that snaps the view back
  behind the bow.

- **Calibration:** during the countdown, point the phone at the big
  screen and tap CALIBRATE. That direction becomes "straight ahead along
  the bow".

- Phone shows the current weapon, ammo left, a flash when a shot lands,
  and a small compass needle showing aim against the bow.

### Engineer: powers and damage control

On screen: seated at the bow with a bucket.

- Two power slots shown as two huge buttons. Tap to use (Shield, Boost,
  Mine, Smoke).

- **Bailing:** Water Cannon hits fill the hull, and a full hull halves
  the boat's speed. When there is water aboard the phone shows SHAKE TO
  BAIL and a water meter. Shaking empties it, and the character bails
  with the bucket on the big screen.

- Stretch: **Ping** reveals every enemy on the minimap for 2 s, then a
  20 s cooldown.

- Portrait or landscape, either works.

### Rules for every controller

- Phones send input 30 times per second, not on every sensor event.

- Android vibrates on fire and on hit. iOS Safari has no vibration API,
  so iOS flashes the screen red instead.

- The screen wake lock keeps phones awake for the whole round.

- The phone background is the team colour with the role name in large
  type, so people can check at a glance.

## 4. Camera, aiming and the target pointer

Each team's viewport is a third-person camera on its own boat, turned
left and right by the Gunner physically turning the phone. The crosshair
never moves: it is fixed at the centre of the view, and every shot
travels flat along the water. Aiming is left and right only.

**Gunner aim (gyroscope only)**

- Turning the phone left or right turns the view and the cannon. No
  dragging, no up or down.

- **Gain of 2:** turning the phone 45° turns the view 90°, so a quarter
  turn of the body covers everything behind the boat. Nobody has to spin
  around in a crowded room.

- **Stabilised aim:** the aim direction is held in the world, not on the
  boat. When the Pilot turns, the Gunner's view does not swing with the
  boat, so a target under the crosshair stays there.

- **Reset:** RECENTER snaps the view behind the bow and clears gyro
  drift. The view also resets behind the bow at calibration and at every
  respawn.

- A small dead zone (about 2° per second) ignores hand tremor.

**Camera**

- Sits about 9 m behind and 4 m above the boat, along the aim direction.
  It looks level, so the horizon runs through the centre of the view and
  the boat sits in the lower part of the frame.

- Steering is always boat-relative: tilt left and the boat turns left,
  whatever the camera faces.

- A small arrow at the bottom of the viewport shows the bow against the
  aim direction, so the Pilot is never confused when the Gunner looks
  sideways.

**Target pointer (crosshair)**

- One crosshair per viewport in the team colour, fixed at the centre of
  the view on the horizon line. It never moves on screen.

- Every shot leaves the cannon at hull height and travels flat along the
  aim direction. All boats sit at the same level, so there is nothing to
  aim up or down at.

- In code, aim is just an angle in the 2D top-down simulation: hits are
  2D rays and 2D projectile checks. Simpler and cheaper than 3D aiming.

- States: neutral ring; red diamond when an enemy is on the aim line; X
  flash on a hit; a lock-on ring when a Torpedo is ready and an enemy is
  in range.

- The Mortar needs no up or down either: it auto-ranges onto the nearest
  enemy near the aim line (section 6).

**Aim assist is required.** Gyro aiming while watching a wall is less
precise than a mouse. Cannon shots bend up to 4° toward the nearest
enemy near the aim line, and the gyro gain drops by 40% while an enemy
is under the crosshair. Both values live in the tuning config.

## 5. Match rules

One mode for the hackathon: **Five-Minute Deathmatch**. One hit sinks a
boat, sunk boats respawn after 5 s with nothing, and the team with the
most kills at 5:00 wins.

**Kills and deaths**

- Any lethal hit sinks the boat instantly: Cannon, Torpedo, Mortar,
  Mine, or a boosted ram.

- The team that fired scores +1 kill and the sunk team takes +1 death. A
  Mine credits the team that dropped it.

- Your own shots, splash and Mines never hurt you.

- The Water Cannon never kills. It pushes boats and fills their hull.

- A Shield absorbs one lethal hit. It is the only way to survive a hit.

**Death and respawn**

- On a lethal hit the boat flips and sinks (about 2 s) and the crew
  tumbles into the canal.

- For 5 s the team's viewport shows a kill-cam on the boat that sank it,
  with "SUNK by Azzurro" and a countdown. Phones show the same
  countdown.

- After 5 s the boat respawns at a random dock with nothing: no weapon,
  no powers, an empty hull.

- The dock is picked at random among the ones at least 80 m from every
  enemy boat (about 16 docks around the map), so nobody respawns into a
  fight.

- 3 s of spawn protection, shown as a bubble. It ends early if the
  Gunner fires, so it can't be abused to attack.

**Hull water.** Water Cannon hits add water to the hull, from 0 to 100.
Speed is multiplied by 1 - 0.5 × water / 100, so a full hull halves
speed. The Engineer shakes it out; 2-person teams drain automatically at
half speed. Slow boats are easy targets, so the Water Cannon sets up
kills without making them.

**Scoring and winning.** A live scoreboard sits on the big screen all
match.

| Order | Rule |
|----|----|
| 1\. Kills | Most kills at 5:00 wins |
| 2\. Deaths | Tied on kills: fewer deaths wins |
| 3\. Sudden death | Still tied: 30 s overtime between the tied teams, next kill wins |

Why kills first rather than kills minus deaths: a net score rewards
hiding in a side canal all match, which is dull to play and to watch.
Ranking by kills keeps everyone hunting; deaths only break ties.

**Round flow**

| Phase | Length | What happens |
|----|----|----|
| Lobby | Until host starts | Join, teams, roles, Enable controls |
| Countdown | 10 s | Boats shown at their spawn docks with crew names, Pilots and Gunners calibrate, 3-2-1 horn |
| Battle | 5:00, fixed | Loot, fight, sink, respawn |
| Results | 20 s | Final scoreboard (kills and deaths per team), top Gunner, best ram, podium with the winning crew, Rematch (same teams) or New lobby |

The closing fog zone from the first draft is gone: it exists to end a
battle royale and has no job in a timed match. Stretch idea in its
place: in the final 60 s crates respawn twice as fast and the timer
turns red.

## 6. Pickups, weapons and powers

Items are scarce and run dry fast, so teams keep moving between crates
all match, as in Blur. Wooden crates float at about 24 fixed points,
each topped by a glowing lantern whose colour tells the category. Drive
through a crate to collect it; it respawns 8 s later with random
contents from its category.

| Crate colour | Category | Goes to                         |
|--------------|----------|---------------------------------|
| Red          | Weapon   | Gunner                          |
| Blue         | Power    | Engineer (Gunner in teams of 2) |

Inventory rules:

- Every life starts empty. Death wipes the weapon slot and both power
  slots.

- The Gunner always has the non-lethal Water Cannon plus one weapon
  slot. Picking up the same weapon tops its ammo back up; a different
  weapon replaces the old one.

- When the last shot is fired, the slot empties and the Water Cannon is
  back automatically. No switch button needed.

- The Engineer holds 2 powers. With both slots full, a blue crate is
  left in the water for someone else.

| Item | Kind | Ammo or duration | Effect | Tier |
|----|----|----|----|----|
| Water Cannon | Default, non-lethal | Infinite | Short-range stream. Pushes boats and fills their hull. Never kills. | MVP |
| Cannon | Weapon | 5 shots | Fast straight shot with mild aim assist. Sinks on hit. | MVP |
| Torpedo (Siluro) | Weapon | 2 shots | Locks the nearest enemy in a 40° cone ahead and homes along the water. Sinks on hit. | MVP |
| Fireworks Mortar (Fuochi del Redentore) | Weapon | 3 shots | Auto-ranged lob: lands on the nearest enemy within 10° of the aim line and 60 m, even behind buildings; with no target it lands 40 m ahead. 6 m splash, sinks on hit. | Should |
| Shield | Power | 8 s or 1 hit | Bubble that absorbs one lethal hit. | MVP |
| Mine | Power | 1, lasts 45 s | Dropped behind the boat, arms after 1 s, sinks the first enemy that touches it. | MVP |
| Boost | Power | 3 s | +60% speed. A ram during boost sinks the target. | Should |
| Smoke (Nebbiolina) | Power | 6 s | Smoke trail that hides you and breaks Torpedo locks. | Stretch |
| Wave (Onda) | Power | 1 use | Shoves every boat within 12 m away, for example into your Mine. | Stretch |

**Ammo.** Five shots is the baseline. Homing and splash weapons get
fewer (Torpedo 2, Mortar 3), because with one-hit kills they would
otherwise decide every fight. All numbers live in the tuning file and
get adjusted at the playtest.

**Counters**, so no item is a free win: the Torpedo is our version of
the Blur Shunt, and Shield, Mine and Smoke answer it. The Mortar answers
hiding in side canals.

## 7. The map: one Venetian district

One compact, invented district that reads as Venice at a glance: about
400 m × 300 m, crossable in roughly 40 s at full speed. It is inspired
by Venice, not a copy of real streets, so we can design it for fights.

**Layout**

- **Main canal:** a wide S-shaped canal (Canal Grande style, about 30 m
  wide) cutting across the map. The open fighting lane.

- **Side canals (rii):** a grid of about 8 narrow canals, 8 to 10 m
  wide, with tight bends and a few dead ends. One gondola fits easily,
  two scrape. Ambush territory.

- **Lagoon basin (bacino):** open water along one edge. Big open fights,
  and the densest cluster of crates, so it pulls teams into fights.

- **Bridges:** 6 to 8 arched stone bridges plus one large covered bridge
  at the centre as the main landmark (Rialto style). Boats pass under
  every bridge.

- **Bell tower (campanile):** tall enough to be seen from every
  viewport, for orientation.

- **Obstacles:** striped mooring poles along walls, a few moored
  gondolas, wooden pile clusters in the lagoon.

**Hiding.** Buildings hide boats in side canals from other viewports
naturally. The shared minimap shows an enemy only for 2 s after it
fires, or while it is in the open lagoon. Hiding is countered by the
Mortar, which lobs over walls, and by the scoring: a team that hides
scores no kills.

**How the map is built.** The whole map is one ASCII grid in
shared/map.ts, 8 m per cell, about 50 × 38 cells. Physics builds its
walls from the grid, and the renderer builds the buildings from the same
grid. This single file is what lets the gameplay and art tracks work in
parallel without waiting on each other.

\# Legend: B building ~ water = bridge over water (visual only)\
\# L lagoon S spawn dock C crate point T landmark tower\
BBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBB\
BBB\~~BBBBB\~~BBBBBBBBC~LL\
BBB\~~BBBBB\~~BBBBB\~\~\~\~~LL\
\~\~\~\~\~\~\~~=\~\~\~\~\~\~\~\~\~\~\~\~~LL\
\~\~~S\~\~\~~=\~\~\~~C\~\~\~\~\~\~~SLL\
BBB\~~BBBBBBBBB\~~BBBB\~~LL\
BBB==BBBTBBBBB\~~BBBB\~~LL\
BBB\~~BBBBBBBBB\~~BBBB\~~LL

Coordinates: metres, Y up, water surface at y = 0, map origin at the
centre. The 2D physics uses (x, z) of the 3D world.

## 8. Physics

Gameplay physics runs in 2D on the water plane, and everything is drawn
in 3D. Boats never leave the water, so a 2D solver gives correct
collisions with far less code and far fewer bugs. This is the biggest
time-saver in the spec.

- **Engine:** Rapier 2D (WASM build) for boats, walls, poles, crates and
  mines.

- **Projectiles:** small custom code (position, velocity, gravity) with
  distance checks against boats. Cannonballs and mortar shells arc in
  3D; only their impact point matters for hits.

- **Timestep:** fixed 60 Hz simulation; the renderer interpolates
  between steps.

**Boat handling (arcade, all values tunable)**

- Rigid body shaped like a gondola, about 6 m × 1.4 m.

- GAS pushes forward; reverse is 40% of forward thrust.

- Strong sideways drag (the keel), so the boat goes where it points.
  Sideways drag drops during a drift turn, so the stern slides out.

- Linear and angular damping act as water resistance. Steering strength
  grows with speed, with a slow turn still possible at rest.

- Top speed about 10 m/s (roughly 3× a real gondola, for fun), 16 m/s
  with Boost.

**Visual-only motion** (costs nothing in the simulation): boats bob on
the waves, roll up to 8° into turns, pitch when accelerating and sit
lower when the hull holds water.

**Collisions and forces**

- Boat against wall: bounce and scrape sparks, no damage.

- Boat against boat: both bounce with real momentum exchange. A boosted
  ram sinks the target; two boosted boats just bounce.

- A lethal hit applies an impulse at the impact point, so the boat flips
  and spins as it sinks. A hit absorbed by a Shield causes a spin-out
  instead.

- The Water Cannon applies a continuous push along its stream.

- Crates and mines are light bodies that drift and can be shoved around.

- Other boats crossing a wake rock visibly.

**Crew physics.** Characters are animated and lean against turns, jolt
on hits and sway with the boat. When a boat sinks, each character gets
an impulse and tumbles into the water with a splash.

## 9. Graphics, characters and audio

The target is convincing Venice at projector distance, at 60 fps with 4
viewports. Realism comes from light, water and materials far more than
from polygon count.

**Look**

- **Light:** golden hour. A warm HDRI sky (Poly Haven, free CC0), a low
  sun, soft haze in the distance.

- **Water:** dark green-teal with animated normal maps, sky reflection
  and foam behind moving boats. No mirror-style planar reflections: they
  double the render cost of every viewport.

- **Buildings** (generated from the map grid): 3 to 5 floors; plaster in
  ochre, terracotta, rose and cream; white Istrian stone around windows
  and along the waterline; gothic arched windows; green shutters; small
  balconies; funnel-shaped chimneys; a dark algae band at the waterline;
  laundry lines across some side canals.

- **Props:** striped mooring poles, arched stone bridges with railings,
  wall lanterns, flower boxes, moored boats.

**Boats and crew**

- **Gondola:** long, black, slightly asymmetric hull with the iron bow
  piece (ferro), trim in the team colour, and one tall lantern at the
  bow glowing in the team colour, so every boat is identifiable across
  the map.

- **Crew:** striped shirts and straw hats with a team-coloured ribbon.
  The Pilot stands at the stern rowing, faster while GAS is held. The
  Gunner sits at the swivel cannon and turns with it. The Engineer sits
  at the bow with a bucket.

- **Animations needed:** row, sit idle, aim-turn, bail, flinch on hit,
  fall overboard, celebrate.

- **Source:** Mixamo characters and animations (free) exported as GLB.
  If importing eats too much time, use simple stylised characters
  generated in code with Fable 5.1. Decide this in the first hour, not
  later.

**Effects:** muzzle flash and smoke, cannonball splash, explosion with a
water column, a boat flipping and sinking, wake foam, the
spawn-protection bubble, a respawn splash, firework bursts for the
Mortar and the podium.

**Audio** (scene PC only, phones stay silent): lapping water, distant
bells, seagulls, cannon booms, splashes, a short accordion or mandolin
loop in the lobby, a horn at round start.

**Performance rules**

- Share geometry and materials; use instancing for windows, poles and
  lanterns; merge building meshes per block.

- Render the shadow map once per frame, not once per viewport.

- Let the haze hide the far edge; simplify buildings beyond about 120 m.

- Measure with 4 viewports by the second checkpoint, not at the end.

## 10. Screens: big-screen HUD and phone UIs

The big screen carries all game information; phones carry only what a
player needs to act without looking down for long.

**Inside each team viewport**

| Position | Shows |
|----|----|
| Top left | Team name and crew names with role icons |
| Top right | Team kills and deaths |
| Centre | Crosshair in the team colour |
| Bottom left | Weapon icon and ammo |
| Bottom right | The Engineer's 2 power slots and the hull water bar |
| Bottom centre | Bow-vs-camera arrow; spawn-protection timer after a respawn |
| Full frame | Blue flash when a Shield absorbs a hit; on death, the 5 s kill-cam with SUNK by and the countdown |

**Shared across the whole screen**

- Top centre: round timer and the live scoreboard, kills per team in
  team colours.

- Kill feed under it, for example "Azzurro sank Verde with a Torpedo".

- Minimap (spare grid cell, or centre where the cells meet): crates and
  enemy boats only while revealed.

**Phone screens**

| Screen | Contents |
|----|----|
| Landing | Two big buttons, SCENE and PLAYER. On a phone, PLAYER is the highlighted one. |
| Join (fallback only) | In-app QR scanner and a 4-letter code field |
| Lobby | Nickname, team colour, role, Swap role, Enable controls, Ready |
| Pilot | Steering wheel graphic rotating with the tilt, GAS on the right half, BRAKE on the left half, team kills |
| Gunner | FIRE over the right two-thirds, RECENTER on the left, weapon and ammo, compass needle for aim against bow. No aim pad: aiming is the gyroscope. |
| Engineer | Two big power buttons, water meter, SHAKE TO BAIL prompt |
| Sunk and Results | Sunk: who sank you and the 5 s countdown. Results: final scoreboard and rematch status |

## 11. Tech stack, architecture and protocol

The scene PC is the game: it simulates, renders and decides everything.
Phones send inputs through a small relay and get status back.

<img src="media/image1.png" style="width:6in;height:3.3125in"
alt="runtime architecture · phones, relay, scene PC" />

runtime architecture · phones, relay, scene PC

Inputs flow right at 30 Hz, status flows back at 10 Hz. The relay never
runs game logic, and the renderer never changes game state.

**Stack**

| Part | Choice | Why |
|----|----|----|
| Build | Vite + TypeScript, one repo, one app | Fast dev server; AI agents know it well |
| Routes | / landing, /scene, /play?room=XXXX | Same app, two modes |
| 3D | Three.js, plain (no React in the game loop) | Most examples available; split screen via scissor viewports |
| Physics | Rapier 2D (@dimforge/rapier2d-compat) | Fast WASM solver, simple API |
| Phone UI | Plain TS with HTML and CSS (React optional) | Six small screens, no build complexity |
| Realtime | Node + Socket.IO relay | Rooms and auto-reconnect for free |
| QR | qrcode to generate; qr-scanner for the fallback scanner | Small, no setup |
| Hosting | Relay on the scene PC, exposed with Cloudflare Tunnel (cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:3000) or ngrok http 3000 | Instant HTTPS URL for the QR, no deploy step |
| Backup host | Render, Railway or Fly.io | Any host running a long-lived Node process. Serverless functions are a poor fit for a WebSocket relay. |

**Contract files.** Written together in the base phase, then read-only
for every agent.

| File | Holds |
|----|----|
| shared/protocol.ts | Every message type below |
| shared/state.ts | The GameState type: the simulation writes it, the renderer and HUD read it |
| shared/map.ts | The ASCII map, legend, parser and coordinate rules |
| shared/config.ts | Every tunable number: speeds, damage, timers, aim assist, ammo, respawn and spawn-protection timers |

**Folder layout** (each folder has one owner, see the plan below)

server/ relay (Node + Socket.IO), also serves the built app\
shared/ contract files\
src/landing/ SCENE / PLAYER choice\
src/net/ socket client, rooms, reconnect\
src/phone/ lobby + Pilot, Gunner, Engineer screens, sensors\
src/sim/ physics, rules, items, kills, respawn, score\
src/scene/ camera rigs, viewports, HUD, keyboard harness\
src/render/ world, water, boats, crew, VFX, audio\
public/assets/ models, textures, sounds

**Messages**

type Role = 'pilot' \| 'gunner' \| 'engineer'\
\
// phone -\> relay -\> scene\
type Hello = { t: 'hello', room: string, token: string, name: string }\
type Swap = { t: 'swap', team?: number, role?: Role }\
type PilotIn = { t: 'in', role: 'pilot', steer: number, gas: boolean,
brake: boolean } // steer -1..1\
type GunnerIn = { t: 'in', role: 'gunner', dYaw: number, fire: boolean,
recenter: boolean } // dYaw: radians since last packet\
type EngIn = { t: 'in', role: 'engineer', use: 0 \| 1 \| null, shake:
number } // shake 0..1\
\
// scene -\> relay -\> phone\
type Hud = { t: 'hud', phase: 'lobby' \| 'countdown' \| 'battle' \|
'results', team: number, role: Role,\
kills: number, deaths: number, respawnIn: number, weapon: string, ammo:
number,\
powers: \[string \| null, string \| null\], water: number, alive:
boolean }\
type Evt = { t: 'evt', kind: 'kill' \| 'sunk' \| 'respawn' \| 'shielded'
\| 'fired' \| 'pickup' \| 'win' }

**Interfaces between tracks**

sim.addPlayer(id, team, role)\
sim.applyInput(id, input) // from phones or the keyboard harness\
sim.step(1 / 60)\
sim.state // GameState, read-only outside src/sim\
sim.drainEvents() // kill, sunk, respawn, fired, pickup, win -\> VFX,
audio, phone haptics\
render(state, events, layout) // one camera per team, scissor viewports

**Sensor notes for the phone code**

- **Steering:** compute it from the gravity vector in
  DeviceMotionEvent.accelerationIncludingGravity (the angle of its x and
  y components, minus the calibration angle). Avoid the alpha, beta and
  gamma orientation angles: they jump when the phone is held upright,
  and alpha drifts. Calibration also absorbs which way the phone is
  turned.

- **Gunner aim:** read DeviceMotionEvent.rotationRate (the gyroscope,
  degrees per second) and project it onto the low-pass-filtered gravity
  vector. That gives the turn rate around the vertical axis however the
  phone is tilted. Integrate it over time, apply the dead zone and the
  gain of 2, and send the change as dYaw. Check the sign on the first
  test and flip it if left turns right. If rotationRate is null (a phone
  without a gyroscope), fall back to changes in the alpha angle of
  deviceorientation, which is noisier.

- **Shake:** count peaks where acceleration without gravity exceeds
  about 15 m/s². More peaks per second means faster bailing.

- **iOS:** DeviceMotionEvent.requestPermission() must run inside a tap
  handl

1	# Gondola Royale: Game Spec & Hackathon Plan
2	
3	Oct 16, 2026 · @Mex
4	
5	## The pitch
6	
7	Gondola Royale (working title) is a party deathmatch for 4 to 18 people
8	in one room. Teams crew armed gondolas in a 3D Venice shown on one big
9	screen, and their phones are the controllers. One hit sinks a boat, a
10	sunk boat is back in 5 seconds, and after 5 minutes the team with the
11	most kills wins.
12	
13	The core loop, in one 5-minute match:
14	
15	1.  Each team spawns at a random dock with empty hands.
16	
17	2.  Teams race to floating crates for weapons and powers, like the
18	    pickups in Blur. Every weapon has only a few shots (5 by default),
19	    so the looting never stops.
20	
21	3.  Teams hunt in the wide canals or ambush from the narrow side canals.
22	
23	4.  One hit sinks a boat. The shooter's team scores a kill; the sunk
24	    team takes a death.
25	
26	5.  Five seconds later the sunk boat respawns at a random dock with
27	    nothing. At 5:00 the team with the most kills wins.
28	
29	Design rules we hold ourselves to:
30	
31	- **Nobody is a passenger.** Every role has something to do every
32	  second.
33	
34	- **The big screen tells the story.** Anyone in the room can follow who
35	  is winning at a glance.
36	
37	- **Zero friction.** Scan, tap, play in under 30 seconds. No install, no
38	  account.
39	
40	- **Death is short, never final.** A sunk crew is back in 5 seconds, so
41	  nobody stands around watching.
42	
43	What changes from the Regata Storica concept: racing is gone. We keep
44	phones as controllers, the big screen, QR join and the HTTPS
45	motion-sensor lesson. The Doge in VR and the printed trophy move to
46	stretch goals.
47	
48	## 1. Platform rules
49	
50	One web app, one URL, two modes. Nothing gets installed anywhere.
51	
52	| Mode | Runs on | Does | Never does |
53	|----|----|----|----|
54	| SCENE | The PC wired to the projector, opened once | Runs the whole game: simulation, physics, 3D rendering, split screen, audio. It is the single source of truth. | Read phone sensors |
55	| PLAYER | Every phone | Reads touch and motion sensors, sends inputs, shows a control pad plus status (role, ammo, team score, respawn countdown) | Render the game world or any 3D |
56	| Relay server | A small Node process | Routes messages between phones and the scene by room code | Game logic of any kind |
57	
58	Hard requirements:
59	
60	- **HTTPS everywhere.** iOS only grants motion sensors and the camera on
61	  secure pages, and only after a user tap.
62	
63	- **Browsers:** Safari on iOS 16+ and Chrome on Android for phones.
64	  Chrome on the scene PC.
65	
66	- **Phone orientation:** landscape for Pilot and Gunner. Show a "rotate
67	  your phone" overlay otherwise, since iOS ignores orientation lock.
68	
69	- **Scene PC:** a laptop or PC with a dedicated GPU, 1080p output to the
70	  projector.
71	
72	- **Keyboard fallback:** every role can be played from the scene PC
73	  keyboard. This is both the dev test harness and the backup if a phone
74	  fails mid-demo.
75	
76	## 2. Joining, teams and the split screen
77	
78	Players join by scanning a QR with the phone's normal camera, which
79	drops them straight into the lobby. One change from the original idea:
80	the QR carries the room link, so phones don't need an in-app scanner.
81	
82	1.  On the projector PC, open the app and pick **SCENE**. It creates a
83	    room with a 4-letter code (for example RIVA) and shows a large QR,
84	    the code and a short URL.
85	
86	2.  Players scan the QR with the phone camera. The QR encodes
87	    https://\<host\>/play?room=RIVA, so the phone opens directly in
88	    PLAYER mode inside that room.
89	
90	    - The **PLAYER** button on the landing page stays as a fallback. It
91	      opens an in-app QR scanner plus a field to type the 4-letter code.
92	
93	    - Why the change: an in-app scanner adds a camera permission prompt
94	      and a library. The native camera skips both.
95	
96	3.  The phone shows a random Venetian nickname (editable) and one big
97	    **Enable controls** button. That single tap is required: it triggers
98	    the iOS motion permission and the screen wake lock.
99	
100	4.  The player appears on the big screen, slotted into a team and a
101	    role.
102	
103	5.  The host starts the round from the scene PC (Start button or Space
104	    bar).
105	
106	**Team assignment**
107	
108	- The host picks team size in the lobby: 3 (default) or 2. Twelve people
109	  in teams of 3 gives 4 teams and a clean 2×2 screen.
110	
111	- Players fill teams in join order. Inside a team, roles fill in order:
112	  Pilot, then Gunner, then Engineer.
113	
114	- Until the round starts, a player can swap role with a teammate or move
115	  to any team with a free slot, from the phone.
116	
117	- Maximum 6 teams, because that is the most viewports a projector can
118	  show readably.
119	
120	- Odd counts are balanced, not left over: 7 players in teams of 3
121	  becomes 3 + 2 + 2, never 3 + 3 + 1.
122	
123	Short-handed teams merge roles automatically:
124	
125	| Members | Who does what |
126	|----|----|
127	| 3 | Pilot, Gunner, Engineer |
128	| 2 | Pilot. The Gunner also gets the two power buttons. Bailing water happens automatically at half speed. |
129	| 1 (stretch) | Solo controller: tilt to steer with auto-throttle, one FIRE button that auto-targets the nearest enemy ahead |
130	
131	**Split-screen layouts** on a 16:9 screen, fixed for the whole round so
132	people don't lose track of their view:
133	
134	| Teams | Layout                  | Spare cell                              |
135	|-------|-------------------------|-----------------------------------------|
136	| 2     | Two side-by-side halves | None                                    |
137	| 3     | 2×2 grid                | Live overview map                       |
138	| 4     | 2×2 grid                | None, minimap sits where the cells meet |
139	| 5     | 3×2 grid                | Live overview map                       |
140	| 6     | 3×2 grid                | None, minimap sits where the cells meet |
141	
142	Each viewport has a thick border in the team colour and the team name.
143	Team colours: Rosso, Azzurro, Verde, Oro, Viola, Arancio. When a boat
144	sinks, its cell shows a 5 s kill-cam on the boat that sank it, with a
145	countdown, then cuts back to the respawned boat.
146	
147	## 3. Roles and phone controls
148	
149	One boat per team, one job per player. The third role (Engineer) is our
150	addition so teams of 3 have a real job, not a spectator seat.
151	
152	### Pilot: drives the boat
153	
154	On screen: the gondolier standing at the stern with the oar.
155	
156	- Hold the phone in landscape with both hands, like a steering wheel.
157	  Rotate it left or right to steer. Dead zone of 4°, full lock at 35°.
158	
159	- Right thumb holds **GAS** (the whole right half of the screen). Left
160	  thumb holds **BRAKE / REVERSE** (the left half).
161	
162	- Hold BRAKE while steering at speed for a **drift turn**: sharper turn,
163	  loses speed.
164	
165	- **Ramming:** hitting an enemy at high speed while boosted sinks them.
166	  This gives the Pilot an attack of their own.
167	
168	- **Calibration:** during the countdown the Pilot holds the phone in a
169	  comfortable position and taps CALIBRATE. That angle becomes
170	  "straight".
171	
172	- Phone shows a big steering-wheel graphic that rotates live with the
173	  tilt. This feedback is essential, since the Pilot is looking at the
174	  wall, not the phone.
175	
176	### Gunner: aims with the gyroscope and shoots
177	
178	On screen: seated mid-boat behind a swivel cannon that turns with the
179	aim.
180	
181	- Hold the phone in landscape with both hands, like a camera, and turn
182	  it left or right to turn the view and the cannon. **Gyroscope only:**
183	  no dragging, no looking up or down. Full rules in section 4.
184	
185	- **FIRE:** the whole right two-thirds of the screen is one big button.
186	  Tap to fire, hold for auto-fire where the weapon allows it.
187	
188	- **RECENTER:** a smaller button on the left that snaps the view back
189	  behind the bow.
190	
191	- **Calibration:** during the countdown, point the phone at the big
192	  screen and tap CALIBRATE. That direction becomes "straight ahead along
193	  the bow".
194	
195	- Phone shows the current weapon, ammo left, a flash when a shot lands,
196	  and a small compass needle showing aim against the bow.
197	
198	### Engineer: powers and damage control
199	
200	On screen: seated at the bow with a bucket.
201	
202	- Two power slots shown as two huge buttons. Tap to use (Shield, Boost,
203	  Mine, Smoke).
204	
205	- **Bailing:** Water Cannon hits fill the hull, and a full hull halves
206	  the boat's speed. When there is water aboard the phone shows SHAKE TO
207	  BAIL and a water meter. Shaking empties it, and the character bails
208	  with the bucket on the big screen.
209	
210	- Stretch: **Ping** reveals every enemy on the minimap for 2 s, then a
211	  20 s cooldown.
212	
213	- Portrait or landscape, either works.
214	
215	### Rules for every controller
216	
217	- Phones send input 30 times per second, not on every sensor event.
218	
219	- Android vibrates on fire and on hit. iOS Safari has no vibration API,
220	  so iOS flashes the screen red instead.
221	
222	- The screen wake lock keeps phones awake for the whole round.
223	
224	- The phone background is the team colour with the role name in large
225	  type, so people can check at a glance.
226	
227	## 4. Camera, aiming and the target pointer
228	
229	Each team's viewport is a third-person camera on its own boat, turned
230	left and right by the Gunner physically turning the phone. The crosshair
231	never moves: it is fixed at the centre of the view, and every shot
232	travels flat along the water. Aiming is left and right only.
233	
234	**Gunner aim (gyroscope only)**
235	
236	- Turning the phone left or right turns the view and the cannon. No
237	  dragging, no up or down.
238	
239	- **Gain of 2:** turning the phone 45° turns the view 90°, so a quarter
240	  turn of the body covers everything behind the boat. Nobody has to spin
241	  around in a crowded room.
242	
243	- **Stabilised aim:** the aim direction is held in the world, not on the
244	  boat. When the Pilot turns, the Gunner's view does not swing with the
245	  boat, so a target under the crosshair stays there.
246	
247	- **Reset:** RECENTER snaps the view behind the bow and clears gyro
248	  drift. The view also resets behind the bow at calibration and at every
249	  respawn.
250	
251	- A small dead zone (about 2° per second) ignores hand tremor.
252	
253	**Camera**
254	
255	- Sits about 9 m behind and 4 m above the boat, along the aim direction.
256	  It looks level, so the horizon runs through the centre of the view and
257	  the boat sits in the lower part of the frame.
258	
259	- Steering is always boat-relative: tilt left and the boat turns left,
260	  whatever the camera faces.
261	
262	- A small arrow at the bottom of the viewport shows the bow against the
263	  aim direction, so the Pilot is never confused when the Gunner looks
264	  sideways.
265	
266	**Target pointer (crosshair)**
267	
268	- One crosshair per viewport in the team colour, fixed at the centre of
269	  the view on the horizon line. It never moves on screen.
270	
271	- Every shot leaves the cannon at hull height and travels flat along the
272	  aim direction. All boats sit at the same level, so there is nothing to
273	  aim up or down at.
274	
275	- In code, aim is just an angle in the 2D top-down simulation: hits are
276	  2D rays and 2D projectile checks. Simpler and cheaper than 3D aiming.
277	
278	- States: neutral ring; red diamond when an enemy is on the aim line; X
279	  flash on a hit; a lock-on ring when a Torpedo is ready and an enemy is
280	  in range.
281	
282	- The Mortar needs no up or down either: it auto-ranges onto the nearest
283	  enemy near the aim line (section 6).
284	
285	**Aim assist is required.** Gyro aiming while watching a wall is less
286	precise than a mouse. Cannon shots bend up to 4° toward the nearest
287	enemy near the aim line, and the gyro gain drops by 40% while an enemy
288	is under the crosshair. Both values live in the tuning config.
289	
290	## 5. Match rules
291	
292	One mode for the hackathon: **Five-Minute Deathmatch**. One hit sinks a
293	boat, sunk boats respawn after 5 s with nothing, and the team with the
294	most kills at 5:00 wins.
295	
296	**Kills and deaths**
297	
298	- Any lethal hit sinks the boat instantly: Cannon, Torpedo, Mortar,
299	  Mine, or a boosted ram.
300	
301	- The team that fired scores +1 kill and the sunk team takes +1 death. A
302	  Mine credits the team that dropped it.
303	
304	- Your own shots, splash and Mines never hurt you.
305	
306	- The Water Cannon never kills. It pushes boats and fills their hull.
307	
308	- A Shield absorbs one lethal hit. It is the only way to survive a hit.
309	
310	**Death and respawn**
311	
312	- On a lethal hit the boat flips and sinks (about 2 s) and the crew
313	  tumbles into the canal.
314	
315	- For 5 s the team's viewport shows a kill-cam on the boat that sank it,
316	  with "SUNK by Azzurro" and a countdown. Phones show the same
317	  countdown.
318	
319	- After 5 s the boat respawns at a random dock with nothing: no weapon,
320	  no powers, an empty hull.
321	
322	- The dock is picked at random among the ones at least 80 m from every
323	  enemy boat (about 16 docks around the map), so nobody respawns into a
324	  fight.
325	
326	- 3 s of spawn protection, shown as a bubble. It ends early if the
327	  Gunner fires, so it can't be abused to attack.
328	
329	**Hull water.** Water Cannon hits add water to the hull, from 0 to 100.
330	Speed is multiplied by 1 - 0.5 × water / 100, so a full hull halves
331	speed. The Engineer shakes it out; 2-person teams drain automatically at
332	half speed. Slow boats are easy targets, so the Water Cannon sets up
333	kills without making them.
334	
335	**Scoring and winning.** A live scoreboard sits on the big screen all
336	match.
337	
338	| Order | Rule |
339	|----|----|
340	| 1\. Kills | Most kills at 5:00 wins |
341	| 2\. Deaths | Tied on kills: fewer deaths wins |
342	| 3\. Sudden death | Still tied: 30 s overtime between the tied teams, next kill wins |
343	
344	Why kills first rather than kills minus deaths: a net score rewards
345	hiding in a side canal all match, which is dull to play and to watch.
346	Ranking by kills keeps everyone hunting; deaths only break ties.
347	
348	**Round flow**
349	
350	| Phase | Length | What happens |
351	|----|----|----|
352	| Lobby | Until host starts | Join, teams, roles, Enable controls |
353	| Countdown | 10 s | Boats shown at their spawn docks with crew names, Pilots and Gunners calibrate, 3-2-1 horn |
354	| Battle | 5:00, fixed | Loot, fight, sink, respawn |
355	| Results | 20 s | Final scoreboard (kills and deaths per team), top Gunner, best ram, podium with the winning crew, Rematch (same teams) or New lobby |
356	
357	The closing fog zone from the first draft is gone: it exists to end a
358	battle royale and has no job in a timed match. Stretch idea in its
359	place: in the final 60 s crates respawn twice as fast and the timer
360	turns red.
361	
362	## 6. Pickups, weapons and powers
363	
364	Items are scarce and run dry fast, so teams keep moving between crates
365	all match, as in Blur. Wooden crates float at about 24 fixed points,
366	each topped by a glowing lantern whose colour tells the category. Drive
367	through a crate to collect it; it respawns 8 s later with random
368	contents from its category.
369	
370	| Crate colour | Category | Goes to                         |
371	|--------------|----------|---------------------------------|
372	| Red          | Weapon   | Gunner                          |
373	| Blue         | Power    | Engineer (Gunner in teams of 2) |
374	
375	Inventory rules:
376	
377	- Every life starts empty. Death wipes the weapon slot and both power
378	  slots.
379	
380	- The Gunner always has the non-lethal Water Cannon plus one weapon
381	  slot. Picking up the same weapon tops its ammo back up; a different
382	  weapon replaces the old one.
383	
384	- When the last shot is fired, the slot empties and the Water Cannon is
385	  back automatically. No switch button needed.
386	
387	- The Engineer holds 2 powers. With both slots full, a blue crate is
388	  left in the water for someone else.
389	
390	| Item | Kind | Ammo or duration | Effect | Tier |
391	|----|----|----|----|----|
392	| Water Cannon | Default, non-lethal | Infinite | Short-range stream. Pushes boats and fills their hull. Never kills. | MVP |
393	| Cannon | Weapon | 5 shots | Fast straight shot with mild aim assist. Sinks on hit. | MVP |
394	| Torpedo (Siluro) | Weapon | 2 shots | Locks the nearest enemy in a 40° cone ahead and homes along the water. Sinks on hit. | MVP |
395	| Fireworks Mortar (Fuochi del Redentore) | Weapon | 3 shots | Auto-ranged lob: lands on the nearest enemy within 10° of the aim line and 60 m, even behind buildings; with no target it lands 40 m ahead. 6 m splash, sinks on hit. | Should |
396	| Shield | Power | 8 s or 1 hit | Bubble that absorbs one lethal hit. | MVP |
397	| Mine | Power | 1, lasts 45 s | Dropped behind the boat, arms after 1 s, sinks the first enemy that touches it. | MVP |
398	| Boost | Power | 3 s | +60% speed. A ram during boost sinks the target. | Should |
399	| Smoke (Nebbiolina) | Power | 6 s | Smoke trail that hides you and breaks Torpedo locks. | Stretch |
400	| Wave (Onda) | Power | 1 use | Shoves every boat within 12 m away, for example into your Mine. | Stretch |
401	
402	**Ammo.** Five shots is the baseline. Homing and splash weapons get
403	fewer (Torpedo 2, Mortar 3), because with one-hit kills they would
404	otherwise decide every fight. All numbers live in the tuning file and
405	get adjusted at the playtest.
406	
407	**Counters**, so no item is a free win: the Torpedo is our version of
408	the Blur Shunt, and Shield, Mine and Smoke answer it. The Mortar answers
409	hiding in side canals.

411	## 7. The map: one Venetian district
412	
413	One compact, invented district that reads as Venice at a glance: about
414	400 m × 300 m, crossable in roughly 40 s at full speed. It is inspired
415	by Venice, not a copy of real streets, so we can design it for fights.
416	
417	**Layout**
418	
419	- **Main canal:** a wide S-shaped canal (Canal Grande style, about 30 m
420	  wide) cutting across the map. The open fighting lane.
421	
422	- **Side canals (rii):** a grid of about 8 narrow canals, 8 to 10 m
423	  wide, with tight bends and a few dead ends. One gondola fits easily,
424	  two scrape. Ambush territory.
425	
426	- **Lagoon basin (bacino):** open water along one edge. Big open fights,
427	  and the densest cluster of crates, so it pulls teams into fights.
428	
429	- **Bridges:** 6 to 8 arched stone bridges plus one large covered bridge
430	  at the centre as the main landmark (Rialto style). Boats pass under
431	  every bridge.
432	
433	- **Bell tower (campanile):** tall enough to be seen from every
434	  viewport, for orientation.
435	
436	- **Obstacles:** striped mooring poles along walls, a few moored
437	  gondolas, wooden pile clusters in the lagoon.
438	
439	**Hiding.** Buildings hide boats in side canals from other viewports
440	naturally. The shared minimap shows an enemy only for 2 s after it
441	fires, or while it is in the open lagoon. Hiding is countered by the
442	Mortar, which lobs over walls, and by the scoring: a team that hides
443	scores no kills.
444	
445	**How the map is built.** The whole map is one ASCII grid in
446	shared/map.ts, 8 m per cell, about 50 × 38 cells. Physics builds its
447	walls from the grid, and the renderer builds the buildings from the same
448	grid. This single file is what lets the gameplay and art tracks work in
449	parallel without waiting on each other.
450	
451	\# Legend: B building ~ water = bridge over water (visual only)\
452	\# L lagoon S spawn dock C crate point T landmark tower\
453	BBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBB\
454	BBB\~~BBBBB\~~BBBBBBBBC~LL\
455	BBB\~~BBBBB\~~BBBBB\~\~\~\~~LL\
456	\~\~\~\~\~\~\~~=\~\~\~\~\~\~\~\~\~\~\~\~~LL\
457	\~\~~S\~\~\~~=\~\~\~~C\~\~\~\~\~\~~SLL\
458	BBB\~~BBBBBBBBB\~~BBBB\~~LL\
459	BBB==BBBTBBBBB\~~BBBB\~~LL\
460	BBB\~~BBBBBBBBB\~~BBBB\~~LL
461	
462	Coordinates: metres, Y up, water surface at y = 0, map origin at the
463	centre. The 2D physics uses (x, z) of the 3D world.
464	
465	## 8. Physics
466	
467	Gameplay physics runs in 2D on the water plane, and everything is drawn
468	in 3D. Boats never leave the water, so a 2D solver gives correct
469	collisions with far less code and far fewer bugs. This is the biggest
470	time-saver in the spec.
471	
472	- **Engine:** Rapier 2D (WASM build) for boats, walls, poles, crates and
473	  mines.
474	
475	- **Projectiles:** small custom code (position, velocity, gravity) with
476	  distance checks against boats. Cannonballs and mortar shells arc in
477	  3D; only their impact point matters for hits.
478	
479	- **Timestep:** fixed 60 Hz simulation; the renderer interpolates
480	  between steps.
481	
482	**Boat handling (arcade, all values tunable)**
483	
484	- Rigid body shaped like a gondola, about 6 m × 1.4 m.
485	
486	- GAS pushes forward; reverse is 40% of forward thrust.
487	
488	- Strong sideways drag (the keel), so the boat goes where it points.
489	  Sideways drag drops during a drift turn, so the stern slides out.
490	
491	- Linear and angular damping act as water resistance. Steering strength
492	  grows with speed, with a slow turn still possible at rest.
493	
494	- Top speed about 10 m/s (roughly 3× a real gondola, for fun), 16 m/s
495	  with Boost.
496	
497	**Visual-only motion** (costs nothing in the simulation): boats bob on
498	the waves, roll up to 8° into turns, pitch when accelerating and sit
499	lower when the hull holds water.
500	
501	**Collisions and forces**
502	
503	- Boat against wall: bounce and scrape sparks, no damage.
504	
505	- Boat against boat: both bounce with real momentum exchange. A boosted
506	  ram sinks the target; two boosted boats just bounce.
507	
508	- A lethal hit applies an impulse at the impact point, so the boat flips
509	  and spins as it sinks. A hit absorbed by a Shield causes a spin-out
510	  instead.
511	
512	- The Water Cannon applies a continuous push along its stream.
513	
514	- Crates and mines are light bodies that drift and can be shoved around.
515	
516	- Other boats crossing a wake rock visibly.
517	
518	**Crew physics.** Characters are animated and lean against turns, jolt
519	on hits and sway with the boat. When a boat sinks, each character gets
520	an impulse and tumbles into the water with a splash.
521

523

525	viewports. Realism comes from light, water and materials far more than
526	from polygon count.

528	**Look**
529	
530	- **Light:** golden hour. A warm HDRI sky (Poly Haven, free CC0), a low
531	  sun, soft haze in the distance.

534	  and foam behind moving boats. No mirror-style planar reflections: they
535	  double the render cost of every viewport.

539	  and along the waterline; gothic arched windows; green shutters; small
540	  balconies; funnel-shaped chimneys; a dark algae band at the waterline;
541	  laundry lines across some side canals.

544	  wall lanterns, flower boxes, moored boats.

546	**Boats and crew**
547	
548	- **Gondola:** long, black, slightly asymmetric hull with the iron bow
549	  piece (ferro), trim in the team colour, and one tall lantern at the

552	
553	- **Crew:** striped shirts and straw hats with a team-coloured ribbon.

625	## 11. Tech stack, architecture and protocol
626	
627	The scene PC is the game: it simulates, renders and decides everything.
628	Phones send inputs through a small relay and get status back.
629	
630	<img src="media/image1.png" style="width:6in;height:3.3125in"
631	alt="runtime architecture · phones, relay, scene PC" />
632	
633	runtime architecture · phones, relay, scene PC
634	
635	Inputs flow right at 30 Hz, status flows back at 10 Hz. The relay never
636	runs game logic, and the renderer never changes game state.
637	
638	**Stack**
639	
640	| Part | Choice | Why |
641	|----|----|----|
642	| Build | Vite + TypeScript, one repo, one app | Fast dev server; AI agents know it well |
643	| Routes | / landing, /scene, /play?room=XXXX | Same app, two modes |
644	| 3D | Three.js, plain (no React in the game loop) | Most examples available; split screen via scissor viewports |
645	| Physics | Rapier 2D (@dimforge/rapier2d-compat) | Fast WASM solver, simple API |
646	| Phone UI | Plain TS with HTML and CSS (React optional) | Six small screens, no build complexity |
647	| Realtime | Node + Socket.IO relay | Rooms and auto-reconnect for free |
648	| QR | qrcode to generate; qr-scanner for the fallback scanner | Small, no setup |
649	| Hosting | Relay on the scene PC, exposed with Cloudflare Tunnel (cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:3000) or ngrok http 3000 | Instant HTTPS URL for the QR, no deploy step |
650	| Backup host | Render, Railway or Fly.io | Any host running a long-lived Node process. Serverless functions are a poor fit for a WebSocket relay. |
651	
652	**Contract files.** Written together in the base phase, then read-only
653	for every agent.
654	
655	| File | Holds |
656	|----|----|
657	| shared/protocol.ts | Every message type below |
658	| shared/state.ts | The GameState type: the simulation writes it, the renderer and HUD read it |
659	| shared/map.ts | The ASCII map, legend, parser and coordinate rules |
660	| shared/config.ts | Every tunable number: speeds, damage, timers, aim assist, ammo, respawn and spawn-protection timers |
661	
662	**Folder layout** (each folder has one owner, see the plan below)
663	
664	server/ relay (Node + Socket.IO), also serves the built app\
665	shared/ contract files\
666	src/landing/ SCENE / PLAYER choice\
667	src/net/ socket client, rooms, reconnect\
668	src/phone/ lobby + Pilot, Gunner, Engineer screens, sensors\
669	src/sim/ physics, rules, items, kills, respawn, score\
670	src/scene/ camera rigs, viewports, HUD, keyboard harness\
671	src/render/ world, water, boats, crew, VFX, audio\

674	**Messages**
675	
676	type Role = 'pilot' \| 'gunner' \| 'engineer'\
677	\
678	// phone -\> relay -\> scene\
679	type Hello = { t: 'hello', room: string, token: string, name: string }\
680	type Swap = { t: 'swap', team?: number, role?: Role }\
681	type PilotIn = { t: 'in', role: 'pilot', steer: number, gas: boolean,
682	brake: boolean } // steer -1..1\

684	recenter: boolean } // dYaw: radians since last packet\
685	type EngIn = { t: 'in', role: 'engineer', use: 0 \| 1 \| null, shake:
686	number } // shake 0..1\

691	kills: number, deaths: number, respawnIn: number, weapon: string, ammo:
692	number,\
693	powers: \[string \| null, string \| null\], water: number, alive:
694	boolean }\
695	type Evt = { t: 'evt', kind: 'kill' \| 'sunk' \| 'respawn' \| 'shielded'
696	\| 'fired' \| 'pickup' \| 'win' }

698	**Interfaces between tracks**
699	
700	sim.addPlayer(id, team, role)\
701	sim.applyInput(id, input) // from phones or the keyboard harness\
702	sim.step(1 / 60)\
703	sim.state // GameState, read-only outside src/sim\
704	sim.drainEvents() // kill, sunk, respawn, fired, pickup, win -\> VFX,
705	audio, phone haptics\
706	render(state, events, layout) // one camera per team, scissor viewports
707	
708	**Sensor notes for the phone code**
709	
710	- **Steering:** compute it from the gravity vector in
711	  DeviceMotionEvent.accelerationIncludingGravity (the angle of its x and
712	  y components, minus the calibration angle). Avoid the alpha, beta and
713	  gamma orientation angles: they jump when the phone is held upright,
714	  and alpha drifts. Calibration also absorbs which way the phone is
715	  turned.
716	
717	- **Gunner aim:** read DeviceMotionEvent.rotationRate (the gyroscope,
718	  degrees per second) and project it onto the low-pass-filtered gravity
719	  vector. That gives the turn rate around the vertical axis however the
720	  phone is tilted. Integrate it over time, apply the dead zone and the
721	  gain of 2, and send the change as dYaw. Check the sign on the first
722	  test and flip it if left turns right. If rotationRate is null (a phone
723	  without a gyroscope), fall back to changes in the alpha angle of
724	  deviceorientation, which is noisier.
725	
726	- **Shake:** count peaks where acceleration without gravity exceeds
727	  about 15 m/s². More peaks per second means faster bailing.
728	
729	- **iOS:** DeviceMotionEvent.requestPermission() must run inside a tap
730	  handler, on HTTPS. One permission covers both steering and gyro aim.
731	
732	- **Wake lock:** navigator.wakeLock.request('screen') in the same tap.
733	
734	- **Reconnect:** keep a token in localStorage; the same token rejoins
735	  the same team and role.
736	
737	## 12. Scope tiers
738	
739	The full spec is more than a few hours of work, even with three AI
740	agents. Build in tiers, and only start a tier when the previous one is
741	playable end to end. The respawn deathmatch is cheaper to build than the
742	battle royale was: no fog, no lanterns, no elimination spectating.
743	
744	| Tier | Includes |
745	|----|----|
746	| MVP (must demo) | SCENE + QR join + lobby; teams of 2 (Pilot + Gunner), up to 4 teams; 2×2 split screen; tilt steering, gyro aim, FIRE; crates with Cannon, Torpedo, Shield, Mine plus the non-lethal Water Cannon; one-hit kills and sinking; 5 s respawn at a random dock with items wiped; spawn protection; 5:00 timer, live scoreboard, results screen; one Venice map |
747	| Should | Engineer role and teams of 3, so all 12 of you play; Mortar; Boost and ram kills; kill-cam; animated crew; bailing by shaking; kill feed; audio |
748	| Stretch | Smoke and Wave; final-minute frenzy; solo teams; the Doge in VR on the Quest 3 as a spectator who drops crates; printed phone grips and a gondola trophy on the Bambu A1 |
749	
750	**Cut order if you fall behind**, first to go at the top: Wave and
751	Smoke, final-minute frenzy, Mortar, kill-cam (show the countdown over
752	the sinking boat instead), animated crew (use static seated poses),
753	Engineer (teams of 2 only).
754	
755	**Never cut:** QR join, steering, aiming, the kill and respawn loop, the
756	live scoreboard, the results screen. Those six are the game.
757	
758	If you want the printed trophy, start the print in the first hour:
759	prints run for hours unattended and can't be rushed at the end.
760	
761	## 13. The 3-person hackathon plan
762	
763	Build the shared base together in the first hour, then split into three
764	tracks that own separate folders and merge to main at three gates. The
765	contract files and the keyboard harness mean nobody waits on anyone.
766	
767	<img src="media/image2.png" style="width:6in;height:3.59821in"
768	alt="hackathon roadmap · 4 phases, 3 tracks, 3 gates" />
769	
770	hackathon roadmap · 4 phases, 3 tracks, 3 gates
771	
772	Durations assume about 6 hours of build time. With less, stop at Gate 2
773	and polish the MVP.
774	
775	**Base phase, all three together (about 1 hour)**
776	
777	- [ ] Create the repo: Vite + TS, the three routes, the Socket.IO relay,
778	  the folder layout. Push to GitHub.
779	
780	- [ ] Write the four contract files: protocol.ts, state.ts, map.ts (a
781	  first rough map), config.ts.
782	
783	- [ ] Placeholder loop: the sim moves box boats on a flat grid from
784	  keyboard input, and the renderer draws them in 2 viewports.
785	
786	- [ ] Start the tunnel and open it on one iPhone: Enable controls, tilt,
787	  and a box boat turns on the TV. This is Gate 1, and the riskiest
788	  unknown.
789	
790	- [ ] Commit SPEC.md (this doc, exported to Markdown) and one TASKS.md
791	  per track.
792	
793	- [ ] If you want the printed trophy, start the Bambu A1 print now.
794	
795	**The three tracks**
796	
797	| Track | Owns | Delivers by Gate 2 (MVP) | Delivers by Gate 3 (Should) |
798	|----|----|----|----|
799	| A. Netcode and phones | server/, src/net/, src/phone/, src/landing/ | Rooms, QR, lobby on both screens, team and role assignment, Pilot and Gunner controllers, steering from gravity, gyro aim, calibration, wake lock | Engineer controller, shake to bail, reconnect into the same slot, haptics and screen flash, HUD feed to phones, backup host |
800	| B. Gameplay and physics | src/sim/, src/scene/ | Rapier boat model, collisions, Water Cannon, Cannon, Torpedo, Shield, Mine, crates, one-hit kills, sinking, 5 s respawn, spawn protection, scoreboard, camera rigs, crosshair and aim assist, big-screen HUD, keyboard harness for every role | Mortar, Boost and ram kills, kill-cam, kill feed, results screen, tuning pass in config.ts |
801	| C. World and art | src/render/, public/assets/ | Venice built from map.ts, water, sky and light, gondola with team colours and its team lantern | Crew and animations, VFX, audio, podium, performance pass with 4 viewports |
802	
803	Who takes what: Track A to whoever knows realtime web and mobile Safari
804	quirks best, Track B to the strongest game-logic coder, Track C to the
805	best visual eye. Fable 5.1 does most of its work on Track C.
806	
807	**Gates.** At each gate everyone merges to main, plays one round on real
808	phones for 5 minutes, and decides what to cut.
809	
810	1.  **Gate 1:** one phone steers a box boat on the TV.
811	
812	2.  **Gate 2:** 4 teams join by QR, loot, shoot, sink, respawn and
813	    finish a 5:00 match on the scoreboard, with placeholder art. Measure
814	    frame rate with 4 viewports here.
815	
816	3.  **Gate 3, feature freeze:** real Venice, gondolas and crew in the
817	    loop; Should-tier features are in or cut. After this, only bug fixes
818	    and tuning.
819	
820	**Working with your AI agents**
821	
822	- One branch per track, and each agent edits only its own folders.
823	  shared/ is read-only for agents: contract changes are agreed out loud
824	  and committed by one person.
825	
826	- One task per agent chat. Give each chat SPEC.md, the contract files
827	  and a single TASKS.md item.
828	
829	- Every feature gets a keyboard or debug toggle, so it can be tested
830	  without phones.
831	
832	- Merge small and often, every 45 to 60 minutes. Pull main before
833	  starting each new task.
834	
835	- Ask for a short "how to test" note in every merge, so a teammate can
836	  check it in a minute.
837	
838	Prompt starter for each agent chat:
839	
840	You are working on Gondola Royale, a browser party game. Read SPEC.md
841	and every file in shared/ first.\
842	Track: B, gameplay and physics. Only edit files in src/sim/ and
843	src/scene/. Treat shared/ as read-only.\
844	Task: \<one item from TASKS-B.md\>\
845	Done when: \<observable result\>, testable with the keyboard harness,
846	and npm run dev runs with no errors.
847	
848	## 14. Risks and day-one checks
849	
850	The two things most likely to sink the demo are iPhone sensors and
851	4-viewport frame rate. Prove both in the first two hours.
852	
853	| Risk | Why it bites | Check and fallback |
854	|----|----|----|
855	| iOS motion permission | Without HTTPS and a user tap, sensors silently return nothing | Test one iPhone through the tunnel during the base phase. Enable controls calls DeviceMotionEvent.requestPermission() inside the tap handler. |
856	| Frame rate with 4 viewports | Venice is rendered 4 times per frame | Measure at checkpoint 2. Cut draw distance, shadows, then building detail. |
857	| Gyro aim feels twitchy or drifts | Hand tremor, slow gyro drift, and nobody can spin 360° in a crowded room | Gain of 2, dead zone, RECENTER, reset on respawn, and aim assist from the first build. Tune gain and dead zone with real players at checkpoint 2. |
858	| Venue WiFi | Slow network or a blocked tunnel | The tunnel goes over the internet, so guest-network isolation doesn't matter. Backup: phone hotspot for the scene PC, or the backup host. |
859	| Character pipeline | Rigging and animation imports can eat hours | Decide Mixamo or code-built characters in hour 1. Static seated poses are an acceptable fallback. |
860	| Merge conflicts | Three agents editing the same files | Folder ownership, read-only contract files, small merges every 45 to 60 minutes. |
861	| Phones sleeping or dropping | A locked screen kills the connection | Wake lock, plus auto-reconnect into the same slot using the token. |
862	| Latency | The tunnel adds a round trip | Expect about 50 to 100 ms, fine for this game. Send input at 30 Hz and interpolate. |
863	| Spawn kills | A boat respawns next to an armed enemy and sinks again before it can move | Respawn only at docks 80 m or more from every enemy, plus 3 s spawn protection. Tune both at the playtest. |
864	
865	**Open questions to settle now**
866	
867	- [x] How many hours until the demo? The plan assumes 6 to 8; with
868	  fewer, stop at MVP.
869	
870	- [x] Is there at least one iPhone and one Android phone in the team for
871	  testing?
872	
873	- [x] What GPU does the scene PC have, and does the projector take
874	  1080p?
