content.content:
## 2. Decisions and why (with rejected alternatives)

### 2a. Lobby and teams (`src/sim/teams.ts`)

**Data model.** `Lobby = { teamSize, teams: string[][], players: Record<id, LobbyPlayer>, spectators: string[] }`. Membership lives only in `teams[i]` (ordered player ids); role is the index (0 Pilot, 1 Gunner, 2 Engineer, `ROLES[index]`). `LobbyPlayer` carries `joinOrder`, `pinned`, `connected`, `enabled` (tapped Enable controls), `ready`, `calibrated`, `kind` ('phone' | 'keyboard' | 'bot'). The same shape is embedded in `GameState` (`teams[i].members`, `players`, `spectators`), so the sim and the lobby share one truth.
Rejected: `player.team` / `player.role` fields. They duplicate the member lists and drift after every swap or rebalance; deriving them (`slotOf`) is O(18) and never wrong.

**Team count and sizes.** `teamCount(n) = min(6, ceil(n / size))`; `targetSizes(n)`: `base = floor(n / t)`, the first `n mod t` teams get `base + 1`. Capacity is `6 x size` (18 in threes, 12 in twos); players beyond it are spectators and do not count in `n`. Full table (verified by `tests/teams.test.ts`):

| n | threes | twos |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | 1 |
| 2 | 2 | 2 |
| 3 | 3 | 2+1 |
| 4 | 2+2 | 2+2 |
| 5 | 3+2 | 2+2+1 |
| 6 | 3+3 | 2+2+2 |
| 7 | 3+2+2 | 2+2+2+1 |
| 8 | 3+3+2 | 2+2+2+2 |
| 9 | 3+3+3 | 2+2+2+2+1 |
| 10 | 3+3+2+2 | 2+2+2+2+2 |
| 11 | 3+3+3+2 | 2+2+2+2+2+1 |
| 12 | 3+3+3+3 | 2+2+2+2+2+2 |
| 13 | 3+3+3+2+2 | 12 playing + 1 spectator |
| 14 | 3+3+3+3+2 | 12 + 2 spectators |
| 15 | 3+3+3+3+3 | 12 + 3 |
| 16 | 3+3+3+3+2+2 | 12 + 4 |
| 17 | 3+3+3+3+3+2 | 12 + 5 |
| 18 | 3+3+3+3+3+3 | 12 + 6 |

Note n = 1..3 in threes (and n = 1..2 in twos) gives one team, which cannot start; `canStart` says so. The spec's range starts at 4.

**Rebalance with the fewest moves** (`rebalance()`, run after every join, leave, size change and manual move):
1. Capacity: if more than `6 x size` people sit in teams (the host lowered the size), the most recent unpinned joiners go to the spectator queue; if seats are free, spectators are promoted in join order.
2. The target multiset is matched to teams by current size, largest to largest (ties: more pinned members first, then lower index). Only surplus people have to move; a team that is already at its target keeps everyone.
3. Teams beyond the target count are dissolved: by construction they are the smallest, with the fewest pins, with the highest index. Surplus teams give up unpinned members first, most recent joiners first (`moverPriority`). So the last person to join is the one who opens a new team, which is what a newcomer expects.
4. Deficits are filled in team order with the pool sorted by join order; a moved player is appended, so takes the next free role and nobody else's role shifts. Surviving teams are compacted and renumbered only if a middle team dissolved (`renumbered: true` so the HUD can re-colour).
Minimality: every person in surplus (or in a dissolved team) must move at least once for the sizes to match the target; the algorithm moves each of them exactly once and nobody else. The join test asserts "at most one existing player moves per join" for n = 1..18.
Rejected: re-dealing everyone by join order after every change (simple, but a leave can re-seat half the room and swap everyone's role). Rejected: leaving teams unbalanced until the host presses Balance (the spec says balanced, "not left over").

**Explicit moves.** `swapRoles(id, teammate)` swaps the two indices and pins both. `moveToTeam(id, team)` is allowed only when `team.members.length < teamSize`; it pins the mover and then rebalances, which may bump one *unpinned* person from an over-full team (7 players, p7 moves into a team of 2: that team keeps 3 because pinned members count in the tiebreak, and the other 3-team gives up its most recent joiner). Pinned players are moved only if no unpinned candidate exists.
Rejected: allowing 3+3+1 after a manual move (contradicts "never 3+3+1").

**Spectators.** A join beyond capacity lands in `spectators` (join order). The phone shows "Spectator, you are next" and the player keeps the lobby screen; promotion happens on a leave in the lobby, on a team-size increase, or at New lobby. During countdown/battle a dropped slot is kept for its token, so spectators are promoted only in the lobby.
Rejected: refusing the join; people re-scan and the host cannot see them.

**Leaving during countdown or battle.** `markDisconnected` only flips `connected`; the seat, boat and score stay. The sim treats a controller with no packet for `net.inputTimeoutSeconds` (1.5 s) as idle: steer 0, gas false, so the boat coasts to a stop and stays a target. Reconnecting with the same token (`reconnectPlayer`) resumes the slot. The keyboard focus (keys 1-6) overrides that team's inputs for as long as the host holds it, which is the mid-demo backup. Removal (`leavePlayer`) is only for the lobby or an explicit host kick.
Rejected: auto-removing and rebalancing mid-match, which would change roles for people who are playing.

**Short-handed teams.** Roles stay Pilot/Gunner by index; `controlsFor()` tells the phone what to draw: a 2-person Gunner gets `powers: true`, and `bailRate()` returns the automatic 20 units/s (half of the Engineer's 40 at full shake) for teams of 1 or 2 members. A 1-person team gets `solo: true`: the sim forces `gas = true`, steer from tilt, and FIRE uses `aimAssist` with the Torpedo-style cone (nearest enemy ahead of the aim). Solo is stretch; the data model already supports it so a late join never breaks.

**Flags and Start.** `enabled` is set when Enable controls succeeds (iOS permission granted), `calibrated` when a calibrate packet arrives during the countdown (reset to false at countdown start). `canStart`: at least 2 teams, each with a connected Pilot (member 0). Everything else is a warning (names shown in orange on the lobby screen), because the keyboard can cover any missing or unready phone and a stuck person must not block the room.
Rejected: requiring every player `ready`: a party lobby never reaches all-ready.

**Rematch and new lobby.** `rematchLobby` keeps teams, roles and pins, resets `ready`/`calibrated`; the sim resets scores, inventories and boats. `resetLobby` drops disconnected players and pins and re-seats everyone by original `joinOrder` (so the same people get the same colours when nothing changed).

### 2b. Split screen and colours (`src/scene/layout.ts`, `shared/config.ts`)

Rects are normalised (0..1) with a top-left origin, which is what the CSS/canvas HUD wants; `toGlPixels()` flips to the bottom-left pixel origin that `WebGLRenderer.setViewport(x, y, w, h)` and `setScissor(...)` expect (the installed `@types/three` 0.186 doc comment says "(x, y) is the lower-left corner of the region").

| teams | grid | cells (team index order: left to right, top to bottom) | spare | minimap |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 2x1 | (0,0,.5,1) (.5,0,.5,1) | none | square 26% of height, bottom-centre, straddling the seam |
| 3 | 2x2 | TL TR BL | BR = overview | inside the spare cell |
| 4 | 2x2 | TL TR BL BR | none | square 24% of height, centred at (.5,.5) |
| 5 | 3x2 | top row 3, bottom row 2 | BR = overview | inside the spare cell |
| 6 | 3x2 | all 6 | none | square 22% of height at the centre |

Cell aspect at 1080p: halves 960x1080 (8:9), 2x2 cells 16:9, 3x2 cells 640x540 (1.19). The camera FOV is per cell, so the halves show a taller, narrower slice; the renderer uses `rectAspect()` for each camera. The top bar (timer, scoreboard, kill feed) is a translucent overlay in the top 7.5% between x = 0.28 and 0.72, drawn over the cells. Borders are `borderFrac` = 0.6% of height (about 6 px at 1080p) in the team colour; the team name sits in the top-left corner on a pill of the team colour with `textColour`.

Team colours were chosen for a projector: bright, saturated, far apart in Lab, and each with a text colour that passes WCAG 4.5:1. Computed with the WCAG 2.1 relative-luminance formula (sources in section 6); the minimum pairwise CIE76 distance is 42.5 (Oro vs Arancio), all others are above 46:

| team | hex | text on it | contrast vs white | vs black | vs dark water #1D4E4A |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rosso | #E53935 | white | 4.23 | 4.97 | 2.22 |
| Azzurro | #29B6F6 | black | 2.30 | 9.12 | 4.07 |
| Verde | #4CAF50 | black | 2.78 | 7.56 | 3.37 |
| Oro | #FFD600 | black | 1.41 | 14.87 | 6.64 |
| Viola | #BA68C8 | black | 3.56 | 5.90 | 2.63 |
| Arancio | #FB8C00 | black | 2.37 | 8.85 | 3.95 |

Rosso and Viola are the darkest against the water, so every border, crosshair and name pill gets a 1-2 px black halo; that is also what keeps them readable when the projector washes out. Red/green confusion is covered by the name on every viewport, boat lantern and phone.
Rejected: the pure CSS names (red, blue, ...): navy and purple vanish on a projector; and pastel sets, which lose the Oro/Arancio and Azzurro/Viola separation.

### 2c. Match state machine (`src/sim/rules.ts`)

Phases: `lobby -> countdown (10 s) -> battle (300 s) -> [overtime (30 s)] -> results (20 s) -> lobby`. `overtime` is its own phase in `GameState` (the viewports and phones need to know), and `phoneHud()` maps it to the protocol's `'battle'` so the spec's `Hud.phase` union stays as written.

Timers are absolute sim times: `phaseEndsAt`, `statusUntil`, `shieldUntil`, ... compared with `state.simTime`, which only advances inside `sim.step()`. Pause therefore means "do not call step" (`paused: true` for the HUD); nothing is decremented, nothing can drift, and a tab that was hidden for 30 s catches up through `sim.maxStepsPerFrame` instead of skipping phases. Abort = `lobbyClock()` plus a sim reset of boats and scores, teams kept.
Rejected: `setTimeout`/`performance.now()` timers: they keep running through a pause and a frozen tab, and they make tests slow.

Transitions (`tickMatch`): countdown end emits `horn` and `phase: battle`; `countdownBeeps` emits `beep 3/2/1` exactly once each even with uneven steps (tested). Battle end: `tiedForFirst` (same kills *and* deaths as the leader) with more than one team -> overtime, else results with `decidedBy: 'kills' | 'deaths'`. Results end -> lobby (rematch-ready) when `match.autoReturnToLobby` is on; the host's Rematch button just calls Start again, New lobby calls `resetLobby`.

Sudden death decisions:
- Only the tied teams play. `overtimeBoatPlan` marks every other boat `status: 'out'`: it is lifted off the water (collider removed), its viewport shows the overview map with "ELIMINATED, watch the overtime", its phones show the Sunk screen without a countdown. Their mines, smoke and projectiles are removed so an eliminated team cannot decide the match.
- Tied boats keep position and inventory; a tied boat that is sinking or respawning respawns immediately with fresh protection, so the overtime never starts with a dead team. All tied boats are revealed on the minimap for the whole overtime (`minimap.revealTiedTeamsInOvertime`): 30 s is too short for hide and seek.
- `overtimeKill` ends the match on the first kill between tied teams (results in 20 s, ranking puts the killer first).
- Still tied at 30 s: `decideAfterOvertime` gives the win to the tied team whose last kill came first (`lastKillAt`, "they got there first"); if nobody scored at all it is a declared draw (both crews on the podium, `draw: true`). One overtime only.
Rejected: repeating overtime until a kill (can loop forever); coin flip (feels unfair on a big screen); keeping eliminated boats on the water as hazards (their kills would have no meaning and their mines would decide the match).

### 2d. Combat rules (`src/sim/rules.ts`, `src/sim/items.ts`)

`resolveHit(target, source, now)` checks in this order: not alive -> ignored; same team -> ignored (shots, splash, mines, rams, including the owner's own old mine after a respawn, because team index is stable); Water Cannon -> ignored (never lethal); ram -> lethal only if the attacker is boosted, the target is not, and the relative impact speed is at least `boat.ramMinImpactSpeed` (7 m/s); spawn protection -> ignored and the Shield is *not* consumed; Shield -> `shielded` (consumed, spin-out); else `sunk` with a `Killer { team, playerId, weapon, pose }`.
Kill credit goes to `source.team` and `source.playerId` recorded when the projectile/mine was created, so a Mine still credits its team after that team has sunk or respawned, and `creditKill` adds the kill to the team and to the player (Gunner for shots, dropper for Mines, Pilot for rams) and a death to the victim team and each of its crew.
Rejected: checking the Shield before spawn protection (a fresh boat would lose a Shield it just looted to a shot that should bounce off the bubble).

Timeline (`sinkTimeline(hitAt)`): status `sinking` until hit + 2 s, `respawning` until hit + 5 s (kill-cam for those 5 s), teleport to the dock at hit + 5 s, `protectedUntil` hit + 8 s. Firing any weapon ends the protection; the Water Cannon too (`weapons.waterCannon.endsSpawnProtection = true`), because the stream pushes enemies into mines and walls and is an attack by the spec's own words ("sets up kills"). It is a config flag in case the playtest shows people losing the bubble by holding FIRE out of habit.

Kill-cam target: the killer boat (team index) while it is alive; `Killer.pose` is frozen at the hit, and the camera falls back to it the moment the killer sinks or respawns, so the kill-cam never cuts to an empty dock. A debug sink (F6) has no killer: the cell shows the countdown over the own sinking boat ("SUNK").

Respawn dock (`pickRespawnDock`): candidates = docks with no boat within `dockClearance` (12 m) and with every enemy boat on the water at least 80 m away; random among them (seeded `rng` for replays); fallback: the free dock with the largest nearest-enemy distance; last resort: any dock. Two boats respawning in the same step pass the first pick in `occupied` (tested).

Hull water: `speedMultiplier = 1 - 0.5 x water / 100`; the stream adds 25/s (a full hull in 4 s); bailing removes `shake x 40` per second on a 3-person team (full shake empties in 2.5 s) and a flat 20/s on 1- and 2-person teams; no natural drain for 3-person teams so the Engineer has a job. Clamped 0..100.

Inventory (`applyPickup`, `consumeShot`, `usePower`): one weapon slot plus the implicit infinite Water Cannon; same weapon tops up to full ammo; different weapon replaces (consumed either way); the last shot sets `weapon = null` so the HUD and phone show Water Cannon again; two power slots fill in order; a third blue crate is `consumed: false` and stays; items whose tier is off are `effect: 'disabled'` and also never rolled. Death: `wipeInventory()`.

Crates: a crate point's category is fixed (`crateCategoryForIndex`: 3 of every 5 map points are red, `crates.weaponShare = 0.6`, because a Gunner without a weapon cannot score). Contents are rolled with weights among the enabled tiers: weapons Cannon 50, Torpedo 30, Mortar 20 (Should); powers Shield 35, Mine 35, Boost 20 (Should), Smoke 5 and Wave 5 (Stretch). Respawn 8 s; 4 s in the last 60 s when the stretch tier is on (`crateRespawnDelay`, `isFrenzy` also turns the timer red).

### 2e. Aiming (`src/sim/aim.ts`)

Aim is one world angle per team (`aimYaw`, radians, bow direction `(cos a, sin a)` on the sim plane; sim `y` is world `z`, final sign conventions belong to `shared/map.ts`). Candidates are the enemy boats that are `alive` and not inside smoke (`hidden`).

- Aim assist: inside a cone of half-angle 8 deg and 70 m, the enemy with the smallest angular offset wins (distance breaks ties), and the shot yaw is bent by `clamp(offset, -4 deg, +4 deg)`. Why smallest angle, not nearest: "near the aim line" is what the Gunner sees; a boat 2 deg off at 60 m is the one they are aiming at, not a boat 7 deg off at 20 m.
- Under the crosshair ("red diamond", gyro gain x 0.6): the aim ray hits the enemy's hull circle (3.5 m) within 90 m; while already on target the circle is 4.6 m (hysteresis) so the state does not flicker at the hull edge. A ray-vs-circle test instead of a fixed angle because the angular size of a 6 m boat changes 3x between 20 m and 60 m.
- The gain reduction is applied on the scene PC when integrating: `aimYaw = wrap(aimYaw + dYaw x (onTarget ? 0.6 : 1) x gyroSign)` (`integrateAim`). The phone sends raw `dYaw` (already dead-zoned and x2 as the spec's sensor note says) because it knows nothing about enemies, the scene is the single source of truth, the same code path serves the keyboard and the bots, and the 0.6 is then a config number instead of a phone redeploy.
- Torpedo lock: nearest enemy *by distance* in a 40 deg cone (half-angle 20) ahead of the **aim**, within 70 m. Along the aim, not the bow: the lock ring is drawn on the crosshair, the Gunner is looking there, and a bow-relative lock would fire at a boat that is not even on screen when the Gunner is looking sideways. Nearest by distance because the torpedo homes (90 deg/s), so angle inside the cone hardly matters but travel time does.
- Mortar: nearest enemy within 10 deg half-angle and 60 m, walls ignored (it lobs); otherwise the point 40 m ahead along the aim.
- Crosshair state from the same facts (`crosshairFor`): hit flash (0.3 s after `hit`) > lock ring (Torpedo equipped and a lock) > red diamond (`onTarget`) > neutral.
- Line of sight: yes for the diamond, the assist and the Torpedo lock; no for the Mortar. A red diamond on a boat behind a building invites wasted shots, and a lock ring on a target the torpedo will never reach feels like a bug. The test is injected (`LineOfSight` callback); the sim implements it with Rapier `world.castRay(new Ray(a, dir), dist, true, QueryFilterFlags.ONLY_FIXED)` (walls, poles and bridge piers are fixed bodies, so dynamic boats never block the ray; verified on the installed 0.21.0: `ONLY_FIXED = 6`, returns `RayColliderHit | null` with `timeOfImpact`). At most 6 teams x 1 ray per step, negligible. Tests use `() => true` / `() => false`.

### 2f. Scoring (`src/sim/rules.ts`)

`compareTeams`: kills desc, deaths asc, earliest `lastKillAt` (a team that never scored sorts after one that did), index asc. `rankTeams` gives the podium order for places 2..6 as well. `computeResults` adds `topGunner` (the player with most kills, any role; ties by join order) and `bestRam` (highest `impactSpeed` of a lethal ram, kept per player in `bestRamSpeed`). Kill feed: `killFeedText` -> "Azzurro sank Verde with a Torpedo", "Oro sank Viola with a Mine", "Rosso rammed Oro", "Verde sank" for a debug sink; `pushKillFeed` keeps the last 5. Minimap: `revealAfterFire` sets `revealedUntil = now + 2` for lethal weapons (the Water Cannon only if `minimap.revealOnWaterCannon`), and `isRevealed` is true while in a lagoon cell (`shared/map.ts` answers `isLagoon(x, y)`), during overtime for tied teams, never while sinking or respawning.

### 2g. Keyboard harness and bots (`src/scene/keyboard.ts`, `src/scene/bot.ts`)

The harness emits the exact `PilotIn` / `GunnerIn` / `EngIn` packets a phone would (`harnessInputs` is pure: pressed codes + edge codes + dt -> one frame), and the scene feeds them through `sim.applyInput(memberId, packet)` for the members of the focused team, so phones, keyboard and bots share one input path. Keys use `KeyboardEvent.code` (physical position: `KeyA` is the A position on AZERTY too), values confirmed against the W3C UI Events code spec.

| key | action |
|---|---|
| 1..6 (`Digit1`..`Digit6`) | focus team |
| A / D | Pilot steer (held) |
| W / S | GAS / BRAKE (held) |
| C | Pilot CALIBRATE (tap) |
| Left / Right | Gunner aim: `dYaw = +-120 deg/s x dt` |
| Space | FIRE (held: auto-fire where the weapon allows) |
| R | RECENTER (tap) |
| Q / E | Engineer power slot 0 / 1 (tap) |
| B | SHAKE TO BAIL (held = shake 1) |
| Enter | Start (lobby) / Rematch (results) |
| P | pause |
| F1 or 7 | debug overlay |
| F2 or 8 | collider wireframes |
| F3 or 9 | free camera |
| F4 or 0 | add a fake team (3 bot players) |
| F5 or - | give the focused Gunner a random weapon |
| F6 or = | sink the focused boat (no killer, feed "X sank") |
| T | toggle bots for all non-focused teams |

F-keys: Chrome binds F1 (help), F3 (find), F5 (reload), F6 (focus toolbar), F11 (fullscreen) itself, and outside fullscreen a page cannot reliably cancel them with `preventDefault()` (reports differ by platform; sources in section 6). Chromium's `IsReservedCommandOrKey` states that in fullscreen "all commands except for IDC_FULLSCREEN and IDC_EXIT should be delivered to the web page", so the harness calls `startFullscreenCapture()` from the Start click (user activation): `requestFullscreen()` and then, where it exists (Chrome 68+, Edge 79+, secure context, JS-initiated fullscreen only, needs a permission prompt since Chrome 130), `navigator.keyboard.lock([...F-keys])`. Because none of that is guaranteed on every PC, every F-key has a plain alternative on the number row (7 8 9 0 - =). `e.repeat` events are ignored (held keys stay in `pressed`), and `blur` clears the set so GAS never sticks when someone alt-tabs.
Rejected: `KeyboardEvent.key` (layout dependent: Z/W swap on AZERTY); making F-keys the only binding.

Bots (`botThink`): read-only over `GameState`, return the three packets plus their memory. Waypoint = nearest weapon crate when unarmed, else the nearest alive enemy, else any crate; steer = `clamp(angleDiff / 30 deg, -1, 1)`, gas unless the target is more than 110 deg behind; stuck (speed < 0.8 m/s for 2 s) -> reverse 1.5 s with the wheel flipped; aim turns toward the nearest enemy at 150 deg/s (sending `dYaw` so the sim's on-target gain and sign apply exactly as for a phone) and fires inside 55 m and 12 deg (Water Cannon inside 14 m); a power every 8 s when it makes sense (Shield under 30 m, Boost under 45 m, Mine under 25 m); shake whenever there is water. Enough to fill 4 viewports with moving, shooting, sinking, respawning boats and to feed the kill feed and scoreboard on day one.

### 2h. `shared/config.ts`

Groups: `teams`, `boat`, `steer`, `water`, `weapons` (waterCannon, cannon, torpedo, mortar), `powers`, `items` (label, tier, weight), `crates`, `match`, `respawn`, `aim`, `camera`, `phone`, `net`, `minimap`, `bots`, `sim`, plus `TIERS`, `TEAM_COLOURS` and `PLAYTEST_TUNING`. `[spec]` marks numbers from SPEC.md; the rest are defaults. `as const` gives literal types for free; `GameConfig = typeof CONFIG` is what every pure function takes as an optional last parameter, so tests can pass a modified copy. Tier gating is one table: `TIERS.stretch = false` removes Smoke, Wave, the frenzy and solo controls everywhere at once.

### 2i. `shared/state.ts`

`GameState` holds phase and absolute timers, teams (name, colours, ordered members, kills, deaths, lastKillAt), boats (pose and prevPose for interpolation, velocity, aimYaw, status and statusUntil, water, weapon and ammo, powers, shield/boost/protection/smoke/reveal timers, killedBy with the frozen killer pose, crosshair state, lock and assist teams, the echoed input for animation), players (id, name, joinOrder, pinned, connected, enabled, ready, calibrated, kind, kills, deaths, bestRamSpeed), spectators, crates (category, contents or null while respawning, respawnAt), mines, projectiles (kind, position, velocity, height for the arc, owner, target, landing point), smoke, kill feed (last 5), results, overtimeTeams, frenzy. `createEmptyState('RIVA')` survives `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify())` unchanged (checked with tsx).
Must NOT be in it: Rapier `World`, `RigidBody`, `Collider` or their `handle` values (the installed 0.21.0 returns handles like `5e-324`, packed index+generation floats that only mean something to the live World and change when the world is rebuilt for a new match), Three.js objects, functions, `Map`/`Set`/`Date`, class instances, wall-clock timestamps, countdown values that would need decrementing, derived data such as `player.team` (use `slotOf`). The sim keeps a private side table `Map<teamIndex, RigidBody>` / `Map<crateId, Collider>`.

`src/sim/hud.ts` projects the state: `phoneHud(state, playerId)` is the spec's `Hud` message (overtime reported as battle, `respawnIn` = ceil(statusUntil - now), ammo -1 for the Water Cannon), `viewportHud(state, team)` has the top-left crew list with roles, kills/deaths, weapon/ammo, powers, water, protection/shield/boost seconds left, `bowVsAim` for the bottom arrow, crosshair state and the kill-cam text/countdown; `sharedHud(state)` has the m:ss clock, red flag (overtime, frenzy, last `match.clockRedLastSeconds` = 30 s), ranked scoreboard and the kill feed strings.

## 2. Decisions and why (with rejected alternatives)

### 2a. Lobby and teams (`src/sim/teams.ts`)

**Data model.** `Lobby = { teamSize, teams: string[][], players: Record<id, LobbyPlayer>, spectators: string[] }`. Membership lives only in `teams[i]` (ordered player ids); role is the index (0 Pilot, 1 Gunner, 2 Engineer, `ROLES[index]`). `LobbyPlayer` carries `joinOrder`, `pinned`, `connected`, `enabled` (tapped Enable controls), `ready`, `calibrated`, `kind` ('phone' | 'keyboard' | 'bot'). The same shape is embedded in `GameState` (`teams[i].members`, `players`, `spectators`), so the sim and the lobby share one truth.
Rejected: `player.team` / `player.role` fields. They duplicate the member lists and drift after every swap or rebalance; deriving them (`slotOf`) is O(18) and never wrong.

**Team count and sizes.** `teamCount(n) = min(6, ceil(n / size))`; `targetSizes(n)`: `base = floor(n / t)`, the first `n mod t` teams get `base + 1`. Capacity is `6 x size` (18 in threes, 12 in twos); players beyond it are spectators and do not count in `n`. Full table (verified by `tests/teams.test.ts`):

| n | threes | twos |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | 1 |
| 2 | 2 | 2 |
| 3 | 3 | 2+1 |
| 4 | 2+2 | 2+2 |
| 5 | 3+2 | 2+2+1 |
| 6 | 3+3 | 2+2+2 |
| 7 | 3+2+2 | 2+2+2+1 |
| 8 | 3+3+2 | 2+2+2+2 |
| 9 | 3+3+3 | 2+2+2+2+1 |
| 10 | 3+3+2+2 | 2+2+2+2+2 |
| 11 | 3+3+3+2 | 2+2+2+2+2+1 |
| 12 | 3+3+3+3 | 2+2+2+2+2+2 |
| 13 | 3+3+3+2+2 | 12 playing + 1 spectator |
| 14 | 3+3+3+3+2 | 12 + 2 spectators |
| 15 | 3+3+3+3+3 | 12 + 3 |
| 16 | 3+3+3+3+2+2 | 12 + 4 |
| 17 | 3+3+3+3+3+2 | 12 + 5 |
| 18 | 3+3+3+3+3+3 | 12 + 6 |

Note n = 1..3 in threes (and n = 1..2 in twos) gives one team, which cannot start; `canStart` says so. The spec's range starts at 4.

**Rebalance with the fewest moves** (`rebalance()`, run after every join, leave, size change and manual move):
1. Capacity: if more than `6 x size` people sit in teams (the host lowered the size), the most recent unpinned joiners go to the spectator queue; if seats are free, spectators are promoted in join order.
2. The target multiset is matched to teams by current size, largest to largest (ties: more pinned members first, then lower index). Only surplus people have to move; a team that is already at its target keeps everyone.
3. Teams beyond the target count are dissolved: by construction they are the smallest, with the fewest pins, with the highest index. Surplus teams give up unpinned members first, most recent joiners first (`moverPriority`). So the last person to join is the one who opens a new team, which is what a newcomer expects.
4. Deficits are filled in team order with the pool sorted by join order; a moved player is appended, so takes the next free role and nobody else's role shifts. Surviving teams are compacted and renumbered only if a middle team dissolved (`renumbered: true` so the HUD can re-colour).
Minimality: every person in surplus (or in a dissolved team) must move at least once for the sizes to match the target; the algorithm moves each of them exactly once and nobody else. The join test asserts "at most one existing player moves per join" for n = 1..18.
Rejected: re-dealing everyone by join order after every change (simple, but a leave can re-seat half the room and swap everyone's role). Rejected: leaving teams unbalanced until the host presses Balance (the spec says balanced, "not left over").

**Explicit moves.** `swapRoles(id, teammate)` swaps the two indices and pins both. `moveToTeam(id, team)` is allowed only when `team.members.length < teamSize`; it pins the mover and then rebalances, which may bump one *unpinned* person from an over-full team (7 players, p7 moves into a team of 2: that team keeps 3 because pinned members count in the tiebreak, and the other 3-team gives up its most recent joiner). Pinned players are moved only if no unpinned candidate exists.
Rejected: allowing 3+3+1 after a manual move (contradicts "never 3+3+1").

**Spectators.** A join beyond capacity lands in `spectators` (join order). The phone shows "Spectator, you are next" and the player keeps the lobby screen; promotion happens on a leave in the lobby, on a team-size increase, or at New lobby. During countdown/battle a dropped slot is kept for its token, so spectators are promoted only in the lobby.
Rejected: refusing the join; people re-scan and the host cannot see them.

**Leaving during countdown or battle.** `markDisconnected` only flips `connected`; the seat, boat and score stay. The sim treats a controller with no packet for `net.inputTimeoutSeconds` (1.5 s) as idle: steer 0, gas false, so the boat coasts to a stop and stays a target. Reconnecting with the same token (`reconnectPlayer`) resumes the slot. The keyboard focus (keys 1-6) overrides that team's inputs for as long as the host holds it, which is the mid-demo backup. Removal (`leavePlayer`) is only for the lobby or an explicit host kick.
Rejected: auto-removing and rebalancing mid-match, which would change roles for people who are playing.

**Short-handed teams.** Roles stay Pilot/Gunner by index; `controlsFor()` tells the phone what to draw: a 2-person Gunner gets `powers: true`, and `bailRate()` returns the automatic 20 units/s (half of the Engineer's 40 at full shake) for teams of 1 or 2 members. A 1-person team gets `solo: true`: the sim forces `gas = true`, steer from tilt, and FIRE uses `aimAssist` with the Torpedo-style cone (nearest enemy ahead of the aim). Solo is stretch; the data model already supports it so a late join never breaks.

**Flags and Start.** `enabled` is set when Enable controls succeeds (iOS permission granted), `calibrated` when a calibrate packet arrives during the countdown (reset to false at countdown start). `canStart`: at least 2 teams, each with a connected Pilot (member 0). Everything else is a warning (names shown in orange on the lobby screen), because the keyboard can cover any missing or unready phone and a stuck person must not block the room.
Rejected: requiring every player `ready`: a party lobby never reaches all-ready.

**Rematch and new lobby.** `rematchLobby` keeps teams, roles and pins, resets `ready`/`calibrated`; the sim resets scores, inventories and boats. `resetLobby` drops disconnected players and pins and re-seats everyone by original `joinOrder` (so the same people get the same colours when nothing changed).

### 2b. Split screen and colours (`src/scene/layout.ts`, `shared/config.ts`)

Rects are normalised (0..1) with a top-left origin, which is what the CSS/canvas HUD wants; `toGlPixels()` flips to the bottom-left pixel origin that `WebGLRenderer.setViewport(x, y, w, h)` and `setScissor(...)` expect (the installed `@types/three` 0.186 doc comment says "(x, y) is the lower-left corner of the region").

| teams | grid | cells (team index order: left to right, top to bottom) | spare | minimap |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 2x1 | (0,0,.5,1) (.5,0,.5,1) | none | square 26% of height, bottom-centre, straddling the seam |
| 3 | 2x2 | TL TR BL | BR = overview | inside the spare cell |
| 4 | 2x2 | TL TR BL BR | none | square 24% of height, centred at (.5,.5) |
| 5 | 3x2 | top row 3, bottom row 2 | BR = overview | inside the spare cell |
| 6 | 3x2 | all 6 | none | square 22% of height at the centre |

Cell aspect at 1080p: halves 960x1080 (8:9), 2x2 cells 16:9, 3x2 cells 640x540 (1.19). The camera FOV is per cell, so the halves show a taller, narrower slice; the renderer uses `rectAspect()` for each camera. The top bar (timer, scoreboard, kill feed) is a translucent overlay in the top 7.5% between x = 0.28 and 0.72, drawn over the cells. Borders are `borderFrac` = 0.6% of height (about 6 px at 1080p) in the team colour; the team name sits in the top-left corner on a pill of the team colour with `textColour`.

Team colours were chosen for a projector: bright, saturated, far apart in Lab, and each with a text colour that passes WCAG 4.5:1. Computed with the WCAG 2.1 relative-luminance formula (sources in section 6); the minimum pairwise CIE76 distance is 42.5 (Oro vs Arancio), all others are above 46:

| team | hex | text on it | contrast vs white | vs black | vs dark water #1D4E4A |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rosso | #E53935 | white | 4.23 | 4.97 | 2.22 |
| Azzurro | #29B6F6 | black | 2.30 | 9.12 | 4.07 |
| Verde | #4CAF50 | black | 2.78 | 7.56 | 3.37 |
| Oro | #FFD600 | black | 1.41 | 14.87 | 6.64 |
| Viola | #BA68C8 | black | 3.56 | 5.90 | 2.63 |
| Arancio | #FB8C00 | black | 2.37 | 8.85 | 3.95 |

Rosso and Viola are the darkest against the water, so every border, crosshair and name pill gets a 1-2 px black halo; that is also what keeps them readable when the projector washes out. Red/green confusion is covered by the name on every viewport, boat lantern and phone.
Rejected: the pure CSS names (red, blue, ...): navy and purple vanish on a projector; and pastel sets, which lose the Oro/Arancio and Azzurro/Viola separation.

### 2c. Match state machine (`src/sim/rules.ts`)

Phases: `lobby -> countdown (10 s) -> battle (300 s) -> [overtime (30 s)] -> results (20 s) -> lobby`. `overtime` is its own phase in `GameState` (the viewports and phones need to know), and `phoneHud()` maps it to the protocol's `'battle'` so the spec's `Hud.phase` union stays as written.

Timers are absolute sim times: `phaseEndsAt`, `statusUntil`, `shieldUntil`, ... compared with `state.simTime`, which only advances inside `sim.step()`. Pause therefore means "do not call step" (`paused: true` for the HUD); nothing is decremented, nothing can drift, and a tab that was hidden for 30 s catches up through `sim.maxStepsPerFrame` instead of skipping phases. Abort = `lobbyClock()` plus a sim reset of boats and scores, teams kept.
Rejected: `setTimeout`/`performance.now()` timers: they keep running through a pause and a frozen tab, and they make tests slow.

Transitions (`tickMatch`): countdown end emits `horn` and `phase: battle`; `countdownBeeps` emits `beep 3/2/1` exactly once each even with uneven steps (tested). Battle end: `tiedForFirst` (same kills *and* deaths as the leader) with more than one team -> overtime, else results with `decidedBy: 'kills' | 'deaths'`. Results end -> lobby (rematch-ready) when `match.autoReturnToLobby` is on; the host's Rematch button just calls Start again, New lobby calls `resetLobby`.

Sudden death decisions:
- Only the tied teams play. `overtimeBoatPlan` marks every other boat `status: 'out'`: it is lifted off the water (collider removed), its viewport shows the overview map with "ELIMINATED, watch the overtime", its phones show the Sunk screen without a countdown. Their mines, smoke and projectiles are removed so an eliminated team cannot decide the match.
- Tied boats keep position and inventory; a tied boat that is sinking or respawning respawns immediately with fresh protection, so the overtime never starts with a dead team. All tied boats are revealed on the minimap for the whole overtime (`minimap.revealTiedTeamsInOvertime`): 30 s is too short for hide and seek.
- `overtimeKill` ends the match on the first kill between tied teams (results in 20 s, ranking puts the killer first).
- Still tied at 30 s: `decideAfterOvertime` gives the win to the tied team whose last kill came first (`lastKillAt`, "they got there first"); if nobody scored at all it is a declared draw (both crews on the podium, `draw: true`). One overtime only.
Rejected: repeating overtime until a kill (can loop forever); coin flip (feels unfair on a big screen); keeping eliminated boats on the water as hazards (their kills would have no meaning and their mines would decide the match).

### 2d. Combat rules (`src/sim/rules.ts`, `src/sim/items.ts`)

`resolveHit(target, source, now)` checks in this order: not alive -> ignored; same team -> ignored (shots, splash, mines, rams, including the owner's own old mine after a respawn, because team index is stable); Water Cannon -> ignored (never lethal); ram -> lethal only if the attacker is boosted, the target is not, and the relative impact speed is at least `boat.ramMinImpactSpeed` (7 m/s); spawn protection -> ignored and the Shield is *not* consumed; Shield -> `shielded` (consumed, spin-out); else `sunk` with a `Killer { team, playerId, weapon, pose }`.
Kill credit goes to `source.team` and `source.playerId` recorded when the projectile/mine was created, so a Mine still credits its team after that team has sunk or respawned, and `creditKill` adds the kill to the team and to the player (Gunner for shots, dropper for Mines, Pilot for rams) and a death to the victim team and each of its crew.
Rejected: checking the Shield before spawn protection (a fresh boat would lose a Shield it just looted to a shot that should bounce off the bubble).

Timeline (`sinkTimeline(hitAt)`): status `sinking` until hit + 2 s, `respawning` until hit + 5 s (kill-cam for those 5 s), teleport to the dock at hit + 5 s, `protectedUntil` hit + 8 s. Firing any weapon ends the protection; the Water Cannon too (`weapons.waterCannon.endsSpawnProtection = true`), because the stream pushes enemies into mines and walls and is an attack by the spec's own words ("sets up kills"). It is a config flag in case the playtest shows people losing the bubble by holding FIRE out of habit.

Kill-cam target: the killer boat (team index) while it is alive; `Killer.pose` is frozen at the hit, and the camera falls back to it the moment the killer sinks or respawns, so the kill-cam never cuts to an empty dock. A debug sink (F6) has no killer: the cell shows the countdown over the own sinking boat ("SUNK").

Respawn dock (`pickRespawnDock`): candidates = docks with no boat within `dockClearance` (12 m) and with every enemy boat on the water at least 80 m away; random among them (seeded `rng` for replays); fallback: the free dock with the largest nearest-enemy distance; last resort: any dock. Two boats respawning in the same step pass the first pick in `occupied` (tested).

Hull water: `speedMultiplier = 1 - 0.5 x water / 100`; the stream adds 25/s (a full hull in 4 s); bailing removes `shake x 40` per second on a 3-person team (full shake empties in 2.5 s) and a flat 20/s on 1- and 2-person teams; no natural drain for 3-person teams so the Engineer has a job. Clamped 0..100.

Inventory (`applyPickup`, `consumeShot`, `usePower`): one weapon slot plus the implicit infinite Water Cannon; same weapon tops up to full ammo; different weapon replaces (consumed either way); the last shot sets `weapon = null` so the HUD and phone show Water Cannon again; two power slots fill in order; a third blue crate is `consumed: false` and stays; items whose tier is off are `effect: 'disabled'` and also never rolled. Death: `wipeInventory()`.

Crates: a crate point's category is fixed (`crateCategoryForIndex`: 3 of every 5 map points are red, `crates.weaponShare = 0.6`, because a Gunner without a weapon cannot score). Contents are rolled with weights among the enabled tiers: weapons Cannon 50, Torpedo 30, Mortar 20 (Should); powers Shield 35, Mine 35, Boost 20 (Should), Smoke 5 and Wave 5 (Stretch). Respawn 8 s; 4 s in the last 60 s when the stretch tier is on (`crateRespawnDelay`, `isFrenzy` also turns the timer red).

### 2e. Aiming (`src/sim/aim.ts`)

Aim is one world angle per team (`aimYaw`, radians, bow direction `(cos a, sin a)` on the sim plane; sim `y` is world `z`, final sign conventions belong to `shared/map.ts`). Candidates are the enemy boats that are `alive` and not inside smoke (`hidden`).

- Aim assist: inside a cone of half-angle 8 deg and 70 m, the enemy with the smallest angular offset wins (distance breaks ties), and the shot yaw is bent by `clamp(offset, -4 deg, +4 deg)`. Why smallest angle, not nearest: "near the aim line" is what the Gunner sees; a boat 2 deg off at 60 m is the one they are aiming at, not a boat 7 deg off at 20 m.
- Under the crosshair ("red diamond", gyro gain x 0.6): the aim ray hits the enemy's hull circle (3.5 m) within 90 m; while already on target the circle is 4.6 m (hysteresis) so the state does not flicker at the hull edge. A ray-vs-circle test instead of a fixed angle because the angular size of a 6 m boat changes 3x between 20 m and 60 m.
- The gain reduction is applied on the scene PC when integrating: `aimYaw = wrap(aimYaw + dYaw x (onTarget ? 0.6 : 1) x gyroSign)` (`integrateAim`). The phone sends raw `dYaw` (already dead-zoned and x2 as the spec's sensor note says) because it knows nothing about enemies, the scene is the single source of truth, the same code path serves the keyboard and the bots, and the 0.6 is then a config number instead of a phone redeploy.
- Torpedo lock: nearest enemy *by distance* in a 40 deg cone (half-angle 20) ahead of the **aim**, within 70 m. Along the aim, not the bow: the lock ring is drawn on the crosshair, the Gunner is looking there, and a bow-relative lock would fire at a boat that is not even on screen when the Gunner is looking sideways. Nearest by distance because the torpedo homes (90 deg/s), so angle inside the cone hardly matters but travel time does.
- Mortar: nearest enemy within 10 deg half-angle and 60 m, walls ignored (it lobs); otherwise the point 40 m ahead along the aim.
- Crosshair state from the same facts (`crosshairFor`): hit flash (0.3 s after `hit`) > lock ring (Torpedo equipped and a lock) > red diamond (`onTarget`) > neutral.
- Line of sight: yes for the diamond, the assist and the Torpedo lock; no for the Mortar. A red diamond on a boat behind a building invites wasted shots, and a lock ring on a target the torpedo will never reach feels like a bug. The test is injected (`LineOfSight` callback); the sim implements it with Rapier `world.castRay(new Ray(a, dir), dist, true, QueryFilterFlags.ONLY_FIXED)` (walls, poles and bridge piers are fixed bodies, so dynamic boats never block the ray; verified on the installed 0.21.0: `ONLY_FIXED = 6`, returns `RayColliderHit | null` with `timeOfImpact`). At most 6 teams x 1 ray per step, negligible. Tests use `() => true` / `() => false`.

### 2f. Scoring (`src/sim/rules.ts`)

`compareTeams`: kills desc, deaths asc, earliest `lastKillAt` (a team that never scored sorts after one that did), index asc. `rankTeams` gives the podium order for places 2..6 as well. `computeResults` adds `topGunner` (the player with most kills, any role; ties by join order) and `bestRam` (highest `impactSpeed` of a lethal ram, kept per player in `bestRamSpeed`). Kill feed: `killFeedText` -> "Azzurro sank Verde with a Torpedo", "Oro sank Viola with a Mine", "Rosso rammed Oro", "Verde sank" for a debug sink; `pushKillFeed` keeps the last 5. Minimap: `revealAfterFire` sets `revealedUntil = now + 2` for lethal weapons (the Water Cannon only if `minimap.revealOnWaterCannon`), and `isRevealed` is true while in a lagoon cell (`shared/map.ts` answers `isLagoon(x, y)`), during overtime for tied teams, never while sinking or respawning.

### 2g. Keyboard harness and bots (`src/scene/keyboard.ts`, `src/scene/bot.ts`)

The harness emits the exact `PilotIn` / `GunnerIn` / `EngIn` packets a phone would (`harnessInputs` is pure: pressed codes + edge codes + dt -> one frame), and the scene feeds them through `sim.applyInput(memberId, packet)` for the members of the focused team, so phones, keyboard and bots share one input path. Keys use `KeyboardEvent.code` (physical position: `KeyA` is the A position on AZERTY too), values confirmed against the W3C UI Events code spec.

| key | action |
|---|---|
| 1..6 (`Digit1`..`Digit6`) | focus team |
| A / D | Pilot steer (held) |
| W / S | GAS / BRAKE (held) |
| C | Pilot CALIBRATE (tap) |
| Left / Right | Gunner aim: `dYaw = +-120 deg/s x dt` |
| Space | FIRE (held: auto-fire where the weapon allows) |
| R | RECENTER (tap) |
| Q / E | Engineer power slot 0 / 1 (tap) |
| B | SHAKE TO BAIL (held = shake 1) |
| Enter | Start (lobby) / Rematch (results) |
| P | pause |
| F1 or 7 | debug overlay |
| F2 or 8 | collider wireframes |
| F3 or 9 | free camera |
| F4 or 0 | add a fake team (3 bot players) |
| F5 or - | give the focused Gunner a random weapon |
| F6 or = | sink the focused boat (no killer, feed "X sank") |
| T | toggle bots for all non-focused teams |

F-keys: Chrome binds F1 (help), F3 (find), F5 (reload), F6 (focus toolbar), F11 (fullscreen) itself, and outside fullscreen a page cannot reliably cancel them with `preventDefault()` (reports differ by platform; sources in section 6). Chromium's `IsReservedCommandOrKey` states that in fullscreen "all commands except for IDC_FULLSCREEN and IDC_EXIT should be delivered to the web page", so the harness calls `startFullscreenCapture()` from the Start click (user activation): `requestFullscreen()` and then, where it exists (Chrome 68+, Edge 79+, secure context, JS-initiated fullscreen only, needs a permission prompt since Chrome 130), `navigator.keyboard.lock([...F-keys])`. Because none of that is guaranteed on every PC, every F-key has a plain alternative on the number row (7 8 9 0 - =). `e.repeat` events are ignored (held keys stay in `pressed`), and `blur` clears the set so GAS never sticks when someone alt-tabs.
Rejected: `KeyboardEvent.key` (layout dependent: Z/W swap on AZERTY); making F-keys the only binding.

Bots (`botThink`): read-only over `GameState`, return the three packets plus their memory. Waypoint = nearest weapon crate when unarmed, else the nearest alive enemy, else any crate; steer = `clamp(angleDiff / 30 deg, -1, 1)`, gas unless the target is more than 110 deg behind; stuck (speed < 0.8 m/s for 2 s) -> reverse 1.5 s with the wheel flipped; aim turns toward the nearest enemy at 150 deg/s (sending `dYaw` so the sim's on-target gain and sign apply exactly as for a phone) and fires inside 55 m and 12 deg (Water Cannon inside 14 m); a power every 8 s when it makes sense (Shield under 30 m, Boost under 45 m, Mine under 25 m); shake whenever there is water. Enough to fill 4 viewports with moving, shooting, sinking, respawning boats and to feed the kill feed and scoreboard on day one.

### 2h. `shared/config.ts`

Groups: `teams`, `boat`, `steer`, `water`, `weapons` (waterCannon, cannon, torpedo, mortar), `powers`, `items` (label, tier, weight), `crates`, `match`, `respawn`, `aim`, `camera`, `phone`, `net`, `minimap`, `bots`, `sim`, plus `TIERS`, `TEAM_COLOURS` and `PLAYTEST_TUNING`. `[spec]` marks numbers from SPEC.md; the rest are defaults. `as const` gives literal types for free; `GameConfig = typeof CONFIG` is what every pure function takes as an optional last parameter, so tests can pass a modified copy. Tier gating is one table: `TIERS.stretch = false` removes Smoke, Wave, the frenzy and solo controls everywhere at once.

### 2i. `shared/state.ts`

`GameState` holds phase and absolute timers, teams (name, colours, ordered members, kills, deaths, lastKillAt), boats (pose and prevPose for interpolation, velocity, aimYaw, status and statusUntil, water, weapon and ammo, powers, shield/boost/protection/smoke/reveal timers, killedBy with the frozen killer pose, crosshair state, lock and assist teams, the echoed input for animation), players (id, name, joinOrder, pinned, connected, enabled, ready, calibrated, kind, kills, deaths, bestRamSpeed), spectators, crates (category, contents or null while respawning, respawnAt), mines, projectiles (kind, position, velocity, height for the arc, owner, target, landing point), smoke, kill feed (last 5), results, overtimeTeams, frenzy. `createEmptyState('RIVA')` survives `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify())` unchanged (checked with tsx).
Must NOT be in it: Rapier `World`, `RigidBody`, `Collider` or their `handle` values (the installed 0.21.0 returns handles like `5e-324`, packed index+generation floats that only mean something to the live World and change when the world is rebuilt for a new match), Three.js objects, functions, `Map`/`Set`/`Date`, class instances, wall-clock timestamps, countdown values that would need decrementing, derived data such as `player.team` (use `slotOf`). The sim keeps a private side table `Map<teamIndex, RigidBody>` / `Map<crateId, Collider>`.

`src/sim/hud.ts` projects the state: `phoneHud(state, playerId)` is the spec's `Hud` message (overtime reported as battle, `respawnIn` = ceil(statusUntil - now), ammo -1 for the Water Cannon), `viewportHud(state, team)` has the top-left crew list with roles, kills/deaths, weapon/ammo, powers, water, protection/shield/boost seconds left, `bowVsAim` for the bottom arrow, crosshair state and the kill-cam text/countdown; `sharedHud(state)` has the m:ss clock, red flag (overtime, frenzy, last `match.clockRedLastSeconds` = 30 s), ranked scoreboard and the kill feed strings.

# HANDOFF: where Gondola Royale stands and how to continue

Written 2026-10-16 by Claude (Fable 5.1) for Makhlug's teammates and their agents.
Read this first, then `SPEC.md`, then every file in `shared/`.

## 1. What exists in this repo right now

| Area | State | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Spec | Committed verbatim (exported from the .docx), with its two diagrams | `SPEC.md`, `docs/media/` |
| Toolchain | Vite 8.3, TypeScript 5.9 (pinned, not 7), Vitest 5, tsx, Socket.IO 4.8, Three 0.186, Rapier 2D compat 0.21, express 5. `npm install` done, `npm test` green (13 tests) | `package.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig*.json`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` |
| Contract files (DONE, authoritative) | `shared/config.ts` (every tunable + tier flags), `shared/state.ts` (GameState, SimEvent), `shared/protocol.ts` (all messages + Socket.IO typed event maps + sanitizers), `shared/api.ts` (Sim and Renderer interfaces between tracks), `shared/map.ts` (the 50x38 ASCII map, parser, walls merge, docks with headings, bridges, lagoon mask), `shared/math.ts` | `shared/` |
| Tests for the contracts | map (connectivity, counts, quays, wall cover), math | `tests/` |
| App shell | `index.html`, `src/main.ts` (routes `/`, `/scene`, `/play` with dynamic imports so phones never load Three/Rapier), `src/landing/index.ts`, `src/styles/base.css` | `src/` |
| Research with ready-to-paste, type-checked and tested code | 4 finished write-ups (sensors, physics, rules, map), 2 partially finished (netcode, render) with their code trees, plus the full agent transcripts | `docs/research/` (see section 3) |
| NOT implemented yet | `server/` (relay), `src/net/`, `src/phone/`, `src/sim/`, `src/scene/`, `src/render/`, assets | folders exist, empty |

`npm run typecheck` currently fails only because `src/scene/main.ts` and `src/phone/main.ts` do not exist yet (the router imports them). Everything else type-checks.

## 2. Decisions that are now fixed (do not re-litigate without telling the others)

1. **One repo, one Vite app, three routes.** Client-side routing on `location.pathname`; the dev server and the relay both fall back to `index.html`.
2. **Coordinates** (in `shared/map.ts`, used by `shared/state.ts`): metres, Three.js frame, Y up, water at y = 0, map origin at the centre, row 0 of the ASCII map is the far side (negative z). The 2D sim uses `(x, z)`. **Yaw = `Object3D.rotation.y`**: forward = `(-sin yaw, -cos yaw)`, yaw 0 looks toward -z, positive yaw turns left. Rapier binding (from the physics research, consistent with this): `sim.x = world.x`, `sim.y = -world.z`, Rapier rotation angle = yaw, the hull's bow is the body's local +y. The map research write-up used a different heading convention (0 = +x, `mesh.rotation.y = -heading`); **that part is superseded** by `shared/map.ts`.
3. **Relay is dumb.** It only understands `host`, `hello`, `in`, `msg`, `to`, `hud` and routes by room code (see `shared/protocol.ts`). Inputs are volatile at 30 Hz; the sim holds the last input; `dYaw` is accumulated on the phone between sends so a dropped packet loses at most one window.
4. **Rooms**: 4-letter codes from `NET.roomCodeAlphabet`; phone token in localStorage rejoins the same slot; the scene keeps its code in sessionStorage and reclaims it; the relay keeps a room 90 s after its scene drops.
5. **Teams**: ordered member list per team, role = index (Pilot, Gunner, Engineer). Team count `min(6, ceil(n / size))`, sizes balanced (7 in threes = 3+2+2). Rebalance moves the most recent joiners first; manual moves pin a player. Beyond 18 (or 12 in twos) = spectators. Full algorithm and tests in `docs/research/rules/final.md`.
6. **Sensors**: steering = `atan2(up.x, up.y)` of the low-passed gravity vector minus the calibration angle; Gunner yaw rate = `rotationRate . unit(up)`; **iOS reports `accelerationIncludingGravity` with the opposite sign to Android/the spec** (flat face up: iOS z = -9.81, Android z = +9.81), so normalise with `sign = -1` on iOS before projecting, and keep an "Invert aim" toggle. `rotationRate.alpha/beta/gamma` are the rates about device x/y/z in that order (what Chromium and WebKit actually do). `event.interval` is seconds on WebKit and milliseconds on Chromium: never use it, use `performance.now()` deltas. Details and code: `docs/research/sensors/final.md`.
7. **Physics**: Rapier damping is `v *= 1/(1 + dt*d)`, so terminal speed is `F/(m*d)`; boat 1000 kg (research) with thrust sized for 10 m/s; keel = scale lateral velocity by `exp(-grip*dt)` via `setLinvel`; ram detection from `COLLISION_EVENTS` + pre-step velocities + `world.contactPair`; sinking = collision groups to a "sinking" mask, then `setEnabled(false)`, respawn by teleport. Colliders become queryable only after one `world.step()`. Details and code: `docs/research/physics/final.md`. Note: `shared/config.ts` in the repo uses mass 400 and its own thrust/damping numbers; either adopt the research's 1000 kg block or keep 400 kg and re-derive thrust = m * d * vTop. Both are fine; pick one and keep `BOAT.topSpeed` true.
8. **Rendering**: one `WebGLRenderer`, scissor viewports per team; `renderer.shadowMap.autoUpdate = false; needsUpdate = true` once per frame renders shadows once for all viewports (verified in three 0.186 source: `WebGLShadowMap` resets `needsUpdate` after one render). HUD as DOM overlays per viewport rect. No planar reflections. Layout rects per `SPEC.md` section 2 (rules research has the exact table and `toGlPixels` flip).
9. **Match flow**: lobby -> countdown 10 s -> battle 300 s -> optional sudden death 30 s (tied teams only, others eliminated) -> results 20 s. Timers are sim-time deadlines (`phaseEndsAt`), never wall-clock. Hit -> sinking 2 s -> respawn at hit + 5 s -> protection 3 s.
10. **Keyboard harness**: keys 1-6 focus a team; A/D W/S C for the Pilot, Left/Right Space R for the Gunner, Q/E B for the Engineer; Enter start, P pause; debug on F1..F6 with 7 8 9 0 - = as fallbacks (Chrome eats F-keys outside fullscreen). Bots exist in the rules research to fill 4 viewports without phones.

## 3. The research folder: what is where

Every file the research agents produced was copied verbatim into `docs/research/`:

| Folder | Status | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `sensors/` | **final.md complete** (~100 KB) | Permission flow, sign conventions with sources, steering and gyro math with numeric proofs, shake, 30 Hz sender, touch pads, wake lock, desktop simulator, test vectors. Code targets `src/phone/*`. |
| `physics/` | **final.md complete** (~120 KB) | Rapier 0.21 proofs, `src/sim/coords.ts`, `geom.ts`, `physics.ts`, `loop.ts`, `boat.ts`, `walls.ts`, `items.ts`, `projectiles.ts`, `sim.ts` order of operations, six test files (all passing in the agent's sandbox). |
| `rules/` | **final.md complete** (~160 KB) | `src/sim/teams.ts`, `rules.ts`, `items.ts`, `aim.ts`, `hud.ts`, `src/scene/layout.ts`, `keyboard.ts`, `bot.ts`, and tests. Also its own proposal for `shared/config.ts` and `shared/state.ts` (richer than the repo's; the repo's are authoritative, lift what you need). The agent's sandbox copy of its typed code is in `rules/shared`, `rules/src`, `rules/tests`. |
| `map/` | **final.md complete** (~94 KB) | The map (identical to `shared/map.ts`), `validate.mjs` (standalone validator, "ALL CHECKS PASSED"), annotated rendering, a parser proposal (superseded on the heading convention only), consumer snippets. |
| `netcode/` | **in progress when stopped; no final.md** | `mirror/` is a working copy of the repo with `server/`, `src/net`, `shared/protocol` drafts, `tests/relay.test.ts`, a load test and logs (`relay-smoke.log`); `proof-relay.ts` proves the Socket.IO forwarding pattern; `proof-express-wildcard.ts` proves the express 5 SPA fallback syntax; `vite-proof/` proves the dev proxy. Read the agent transcript for its conclusions (see below). |
| `render/` | **in progress when stopped; no final.md** | `code/src/render/*`, `code/src/scene/*`, `code/tests/{buildings,camera,layout}.test.ts`, `proof-exports.mjs` (verified three 0.186 addon exports). Read the transcript for the write-up it had drafted. |
| `_workflow/` | complete | The workflow script and every agent transcript (`agent-*.jsonl`, one JSON object per line; `*.meta.json` names the topic). The netcode agent is `agent-afab987e3f456c9ce`, render is `agent-a71c3c61ab65370a0`, sensors `agent-a3805393801a5924b`, physics `agent-a52d0d07d5b35ee55`, rules `agent-a3ceb19eef51e2aa4`, map `agent-abc575981e5c22b0b`. The other three are verification agents that had just started. |

To pull a draft out of a transcript, grep for the `Write` tool calls:
```bash
grep -o '"name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"[^"]*"' docs/research/_workflow/agent-afab987e3f456c9ce.jsonl | sort -u
```
and the file contents are in the same JSON lines (`"content":`).

## 4. Known gaps and mismatches to resolve first

- `src/scene/main.ts` and `src/phone/main.ts` are missing: write them first so `npm run typecheck` and `npm run dev` work.
- The research code was written against each agent's own copy of `shared/*`; adapt imports and names to the repo's `shared/` (`BOAT`, `AIM`, `WEAPONS`, `GameState` fields, `InputPacket` with `seq`). Expect an hour of reconciliation per track, not more; the logic is done.
- `shared/state.ts` has `BoatState.status: 'alive' | 'sinking' | 'respawning'`; the rules research adds `'out'` for teams eliminated in sudden death. Add it if you implement sudden death.
- The research `Hud` adds `overtime` as its own phase and reports it as `'battle'` to phones; the repo's `Phase` already includes `'suddendeath'`. Either is fine; keep `shared/protocol.ts` as the truth.
- Nobody has run anything in a browser yet. Gate 1 (one phone steers a box boat) is still the first thing to prove.
- Assets: none yet. See `docs/ASSETS.md` for the sound list and the image prompts.

## 5. Suggested order of work (three laptops, three agents)

Base (together, 1 hour): write `src/scene/main.ts` (loop: fixed 60 Hz sim step with accumulator, render with alpha, keyboard harness) and `src/phone/main.ts` (join, lobby, role screens) as thin shells; write `server/index.ts` from `docs/research/netcode/mirror/server`; get a box boat moving from the keyboard in two viewports; start the tunnel and test one iPhone. Then split:

- **Track A (server/, src/net/, src/phone/, src/landing/)**: `docs/TASKS-A.md`. Lift from `docs/research/netcode/mirror` and `docs/research/sensors/final.md`.
- **Track B (src/sim/, src/scene/)**: `docs/TASKS-B.md`. Lift from `docs/research/physics/final.md` and `docs/research/rules/final.md`.
- **Track C (src/render/, public/assets/)**: `docs/TASKS-C.md`. Lift from `docs/research/render/code` and the render transcript; assets per `docs/ASSETS.md`.

`shared/` is read-only for agents. A contract change is agreed out loud and committed by one person, with the tests in `tests/` updated.

## 6. Prompt starter for an agent chat

```
You are working on Gondola Royale, a browser party game. Read SPEC.md, HANDOFF.md and every file in shared/ first.
Track: B, gameplay and physics. Only edit files in src/sim/ and src/scene/. Treat shared/ as read-only.
Ready-made, tested code for this track is in docs/research/physics/final.md and docs/research/rules/final.md; adapt it to the repo's shared/ types instead of rewriting it.
Task: <one item from docs/TASKS-B.md>
Done when: <observable result>, testable with the keyboard harness, and `npm run check` passes.
```

## 7. Commands

```bash
npm install
npm run dev          # Vite on :5173 + relay on :3000 (proxied), open http://localhost:5173
npm run check        # typecheck + tests + build
npm run tunnel       # cloudflared quick tunnel to :5173 (install: brew install cloudflared)
npm run preview      # production build served by the relay on :3000
```

## Quick start

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

## Scripts

| Script | Does |
|---|---|
| `npm run dev` | Vite dev server (5173) + relay (3000, proxied under `/socket.io`) |
| `npm run check` | typecheck, tests, production build |
| `npm test` | Vitest |
| `npm run build` / `npm start` | Build to `dist/` and serve it from the relay on 3000 |
| `npm run tunnel` | Cloudflare quick tunnel to the dev server (HTTPS URL for phones) |

| Folder | Owner | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `shared/` | everyone, read-only for agents | contract files: config, state, protocol, api, map, math |
| `server/` | Track A | Socket.IO relay, serves `dist/` in production |
| `src/net/` | Track A | socket client for phones and the scene, token, reconnect |
| `src/phone/` | Track A | lobby, Pilot / Gunner / Engineer screens, sensors |
| `src/landing/` | Track A | SCENE / PLAYER choice |
| `src/sim/` | Track B | Rapier physics, rules, items, kills, respawn, score |
| `src/scene/` | Track B | game loop, camera rigs, viewports, HUD, keyboard harness |
| `src/render/` | Track C | world, water, boats, crew, VFX, audio |
| `public/assets/` | Track C | models, textures, sounds |
| `tests/` | the folder's owner | Vitest, node environment |

Rules: one branch per track, merge to `main` small and often (every 45 to 60 minutes), pull `main` before each new task, every merge comes with a two-line "how to test". Every feature has a keyboard or debug toggle so it can be tested without phones.

## Routes

`/` landing, `/scene` the projector PC, `/play?room=CODE` a phone. One Vite app; each route is a dynamic import so phones never download Three.js or Rapier.

Owns `src/sim/`, `src/scene/`. Read `HANDOFF.md`, `shared/api.ts`, `shared/state.ts`, `shared/config.ts`, `shared/map.ts` first. Ready-made, tested code: `docs/research/physics/final.md` (coords, geom, physics, loop, boat, walls, items, projectiles, step order, six test files) and `docs/research/rules/final.md` (teams, rules, items, aim, hud, layout, keyboard, bot, tests). Adapt it to the repo's `shared/` types; do not rewrite it.

## Base (with everyone)

- [ ] B1 `src/scene/main.ts`: canvas, layout from team count (`src/scene/layout.ts`), `Sim` + `Renderer` wiring, fixed 60 Hz accumulator with `SIM.maxStepsPerFrame`, interpolation alpha, keyboard harness, Start on Enter/Space. Done: `npm run dev` shows two viewports with box boats.
- [ ] B2 `src/sim/index.ts` implementing `Sim` from `shared/api.ts` with Rapier loaded by dynamic import (`await RAPIER.init()`), walls from `getMap().walls`, one boat per team, `applyInput` holding the last packet and dropping stale `seq`. Done: keyboard drives a box boat; it bounces off walls.

## MVP (Gate 2)

- [ ] B3 Boat model (`src/sim/boat.ts`): thrust, reverse 40%, keel grip, drift on BRAKE + steer, speed-scaled steering torque, turn-rate cap, top speed 10 m/s reached in about 3 s, hull-water slowdown. Done: `tests/sim/boat.test.ts` (top speed, keel decay).
- [ ] B4 Lobby and teams (`src/sim/teams.ts`): ordered members, balanced sizes, rebalance with fewest moves, swap/move/pin, spectators, `canStart`, `lobbySnapshot()`. Done: `tests/teams.test.ts` balance table for n = 1..18, both sizes.
- [ ] B5 Match flow (`src/sim/rules.ts`): lobby -> countdown 10 s (beeps, horn) -> battle 300 s -> results 20 s; rematch / new lobby / abort / pause; sim-time deadlines only.
- [ ] B6 Water Cannon, Cannon, Torpedo (`src/sim/projectiles.ts`): 2D hit tests, `castRay` wall blocking, torpedo lock and homing; `fired` / `hit` / `splash` events.
- [ ] B7 Crates and inventory (`src/sim/items.ts`): red/blue categories, weighted contents by tier flags, pickup on touch, 8 s respawn, same-weapon tops up, last shot -> Water Cannon, two power slots.
- [ ] B8 Shield and Mine; lethal-hit resolution order (dead -> own team -> water cannon -> ram rule -> spawn protection -> shield -> sunk); kill credit; death wipes inventory.
- [ ] B9 Sinking and respawn: 2 s sinking (collision mask), respawn at hit + 5 s at a dock >= 80 m from every enemy (fallback farthest), 3 s protection ending on fire; kill-cam target with frozen killer pose.
- [ ] B10 Aim (`src/sim/aim.ts`): world aim yaw, RECENTER, reset on respawn, aim assist bend <= 4 deg, under-crosshair gain x0.6 applied when integrating `dYaw`, torpedo lock cone 40 deg, line-of-sight rays; crosshair state.
- [ ] B11 Scoreboard and HUD data (`src/sim/hud.ts`, `src/scene/hud.ts`): per-viewport HUD (crew, kills/deaths, crosshair, weapon/ammo, powers, water bar, bow-vs-aim arrow, protection timer, SUNK overlay) and the shared top bar (timer, scoreboard), phone `Hud` at 10 Hz via `src/net/host.ts`.
- [ ] B12 Camera rig (`src/scene/camera.ts`): 9 m back, 4 m up along the aim yaw, level look, smoothing on position only, kill-cam, `CameraView[]` for the renderer.
- [ ] B13 Keyboard harness (`src/scene/keyboard.ts`): all roles for the focused team, globals, debug toggles, number-row fallbacks for F-keys; bots (`src/scene/bot.ts`) to fill viewports.
- [ ] B14 Results screen: ranking, kills/deaths, top Gunner, best ram, Rematch / New lobby.

## Should (Gate 3)

- [ ] B15 Mortar: auto-range (10 deg, 60 m, else 40 m), 1.6 s flight, 6 m splash, no wall check.
- [ ] B16 Boost and ram kills from contact events + pre-step velocities; two boosted boats bounce.
- [ ] B17 Kill feed (last 5), minimap reveal rule (2 s after firing, always in the lagoon), kill-cam polish.
- [ ] B18 Engineer: bailing from `shake`, auto-drain at half rate for 2-person teams; Gunner powers in teams of 2.
- [ ] B19 Sudden death (tied teams only), results extras, tuning pass on `shared/config.ts` (see `PLAYTEST_TUNING`).

## Measure at Gate 2

Frame rate with 4 viewports and 4 bot teams on the scene PC, `renderer.info` draw calls per viewport, sim step time (should be under 1 ms).

# TASKS-C: world and art

Owns `src/render/`, `public/assets/`. Read `HANDOFF.md`, `shared/api.ts` (the `Renderer` interface and `Layout`), `shared/state.ts`, `shared/map.ts` first. Ready-made code: `docs/research/render/code/src/render`, `docs/research/render/code/src/scene`, `docs/research/render/code/tests` (buildings, camera, layout) and the render agent transcript `docs/research/_workflow/agent-a71c3c61ab65370a0.jsonl` (its draft write-up). Assets: `docs/ASSETS.md`.

Decide in the first hour: Mixamo GLB crew or code-built stylised crew. Recommendation from the research: code-built capsule characters with procedural animation for the hackathon; GLB as the upgrade path.

## Base (with everyone)

- [ ] C1 `src/render/index.ts` implementing `Renderer`: one `WebGLRenderer`, scissor viewports from `Layout.cells`, one camera per `CameraView`, `autoClear` once per frame, DPR capped at 1, resize. Box boats and a flat grid. Done: two viewports show two moving boxes driven by the sim.

## MVP (Gate 2)

- [ ] C2 World from the map (`src/render/world.ts`): building blocks from `map.walls` (3 to 5 floors, plaster colours, stone band and algae band at the waterline), merged per block; windows and shutters as `InstancedMesh`; bridges from `map.bridges` (arch generator, the covered bridge with a roof), the campanile at `map.tower`, mooring poles, pile clusters at `map.piles`, the lagoon edge as a breakwater.
- [ ] C3 Water (`src/render/water.ts`): large plane, two scrolling normal maps, HDRI env reflection, dark green-teal, foam wake behind boats. No planar reflections.
- [ ] C4 Sky and light (`src/render/sky.ts`): golden-hour HDRI via `RGBELoader` + `PMREMGenerator`, low sun `DirectionalLight` with one shadow pass per frame (`shadowMap.autoUpdate = false; needsUpdate = true` once per frame), hemisphere fill, ACES tone mapping, fog from `CAMERA.fogNear/fogFar`.
- [ ] C5 Gondola (`src/render/boats.ts`): black asymmetric hull (lathe/extrude, bow along -z), ferro, trim and bow lantern in the team colour (emissive + sprite glow, no point lights), bob/roll/pitch from speed and steer, sits lower with hull water; sinking flip from `status === 'sinking'`.
- [ ] C6 Crates with coloured lanterns, mines, cannonballs with the visual arc (`ProjectileState.y`), torpedo wake, spawn-protection bubble.

# The hard parts and their solutions

Each entry: the risk, the decision, and where the full write-up with code lives in `docs/research/`.

## 1. iOS motion permission and HTTPS

Risk: without HTTPS and a user tap, sensors silently return nothing.
Solution: the single **Enable controls** tap calls `DeviceMotionEvent.requestPermission()` (and the orientation one for the fallback), requests the wake lock and, on Android, fullscreen + landscape lock; a 1.5 s watchdog shows a clear error when no `devicemotion` event arrives (HTTP page, denied permission, desktop). HTTPS comes from the tunnel (`npm run tunnel`, Cloudflare quick tunnel supports WebSockets, random URL per run, the QR is generated at runtime from `location.origin`); LAN alternative `npm run dev:https` with a self-signed cert (phones must accept the warning). Write-up: `docs/research/sensors/final.md` sections 2 (D3, D7) and 4; hosting in the netcode agent transcript.

## 2. Steering from the gravity vector

Solution: `phi = atan2(up.x, up.y)` of the low-passed (80 ms) gravity vector; `steer` from `wrap(phi_cal - phi)` with a 4 deg dead zone, full lock at 35 deg and a `0.6x + 0.4x^3` curve. Exact at any pitch; both landscape orientations and the iOS sign inversion only shift the calibration offset. Numeric proofs and test vectors: `docs/research/sensors/final.md` section 3.1.

## 3. Gyro aim that is not twitchy and does not drift

Solution: yaw rate = `rotationRate . unit(up)` (projection onto the world vertical), `rotationRate.alpha/beta/gamma` being the rates about device x/y/z in that order (what browsers actually do, not the old spec text); dead zone 2 deg/s, gain 2, integrated into `dYaw` between 30 Hz sends; RECENTER and respawn reset the sim's aim; the scene applies the 40 % gain drop while an enemy is under the crosshair; aim assist bends shots up to 4 deg. **iOS reports `accelerationIncludingGravity` with the opposite sign** (flat: z = -9.81), so normalise with `sign = -1` on iOS, confirmed by a physics detector during the lobby, with an "Invert aim" toggle as the last resort. Write-up: `docs/research/sensors/final.md` D2, D3, D9; aiming rules in `docs/research/rules/final.md` 2e.

## 4. Frame rate with 4 viewports

Solution: one renderer, scissor viewports, **one shadow pass per frame** (`shadowMap.autoUpdate = false`, `needsUpdate = true` before the first viewport; verified in three 0.186 `WebGLShadowMap`), DPR 1 (each cell is 960x540 at 1080p), merged building blocks, instanced windows/poles/lanterns, fog hiding beyond 120 m, no planar water reflections, no point lights on lanterns, Canvas 2D for the minimap and overview. Measure at Gate 2 with 4 bot teams. Write-up: render agent transcript and `docs/research/render/code`.

## 5. The relay, rooms and reconnect

Solution: the relay only routes (`host`, `hello`, `in`, `msg`, `to`, `hud`); inputs volatile at 30 Hz, HUD volatile at 10 Hz per player, roster reliable; token in localStorage rejoins the same slot, the scene reclaims its room code from sessionStorage, 90 s grace after the scene drops; every packet sanitised and rate limited; express 5 SPA fallback; Vite proxies `/socket.io` with `ws: true`. Contract: `shared/protocol.ts`. Proofs and a working relay draft: `docs/research/netcode/`.

## 6. Boat physics that feels arcade and stays stable

Solution: Rapier 2D 0.21 with `y := -z` so the Rapier angle equals the Three.js yaw; damping `v *= 1/(1 + dt d)` gives terminal speed `F/(m d)` (thrust derived from the top speed); keel by scaling lateral velocity `exp(-grip dt)`; steering torque from the steady-state turn rate; ram detection from collision events plus pre-step velocities and `contactPair`; sinking by collision mask, respawn by teleport; projectiles as plain objects with segment-vs-OBB tests and `castRay` for walls. Write-up and tested code: `docs/research/physics/final.md`.

## 7. The map as one ASCII grid

Solution: `shared/map.ts` holds the 50x38 grid; greedy rectangle merge gives 69 wall colliders; docks face the longest run of open water; bridges are water for physics; the lagoon mask drives the minimap reveal; `npm test` fails on any structural break (connectivity, counts, quays). Validator and measurements (Monte Carlo on the 80 m respawn rule: a candidate dock always exists): `docs/research/map/`.

## 8. Teams that stay balanced and roles that never block

Solution: ordered members, role = index; `min(6, ceil(n / size))` teams with balanced sizes; rebalance moves the most recent joiners first and keeps manual moves pinned; spectators beyond capacity; Start needs only two teams with a connected Pilot (the keyboard covers anyone). Full algorithm, table for n = 1..18 and tests: `docs/research/rules/final.md` 2a.

## 9. Spawn kills, ties and the kill-cam

Solution: respawn only at docks >= 80 m from every enemy (fallback: farthest), 3 s protection that ends on fire; ranking by kills then deaths, one 30 s sudden death between the tied teams only; kill-cam on the killer with its pose frozen at the hit so the camera never cuts to an empty dock. `docs/research/rules/final.md` 2c, 2d.

## 10. Three agents without merge conflicts

Solution: folder ownership (README), `shared/` read-only, every feature behind a keyboard or debug toggle, one task per agent chat with the prompt starter in `HANDOFF.md`, merges every 45 to 60 minutes with a "how to test" note.

# Assets: sounds to download, images to generate

Everything lives under `public/assets/`. The filenames below are the ones the code should load; keep them so Track C's loaders and the agents agree. Prefer CC0 sources (no attribution needed on the big screen).

## Sounds (download, CC0)

Put them in `public/assets/sounds/`, OGG or MP3, mono, 44.1 kHz, trimmed, normalised to about -3 dB.

| File | Used for | Where to get it (search terms) |
|---|---|---|
| `water-lapping.ogg` | ambient loop on the scene | freesound.org "water lapping gentle loop" (CC0 filter); or Kenney "Nature Sounds" pack |
| `seagulls.ogg` | ambient, sparse | freesound.org "seagulls distant" CC0 |
| `bells-distant.ogg` | ambient, every 60 to 90 s | freesound.org "church bells distant" CC0 |
| `cannon.ogg` | Cannon shot | freesound.org "cannon shot" CC0, or Kenney "Impact Sounds" |
| `torpedo-launch.ogg` | Torpedo launch | freesound.org "whoosh underwater" CC0 |
| `mortar-launch.ogg`, `firework-burst.ogg` | Mortar | freesound.org "firework launch", "firework explosion" CC0 |
| `water-cannon.ogg` | stream loop while FIRE is held | freesound.org "hose spray loop" CC0 |
| `splash-small.ogg`, `splash-big.ogg` | cannonball splash, sinking | freesound.org "water splash" CC0 |
| `explosion-water.ogg` | lethal hit | freesound.org "explosion water" CC0 |
| `shield-up.ogg`, `shield-hit.ogg` | Shield | Kenney "Sci-fi Sounds" (CC0) |
| `pickup.ogg` | crate collected | Kenney "Digital Audio" pack |
| `wood-scrape.ogg`, `wood-bump.ogg` | wall scrape, boat bump | freesound.org "wood creak", "boat hull bump" CC0 |
| `horn.ogg` | round start | freesound.org "ship horn" CC0 |
| `beep.ogg` | countdown 3-2-1 | Kenney "UI Audio" |
| `lobby-loop.ogg` | accordion or mandolin loop in the lobby | freemusicarchive.org or pixabay.com music, "italian accordion" (check the licence allows public performance) |
| `win-fanfare.ogg` | podium | pixabay.com sound effects "fanfare" |

Kenney packs: https://kenney.nl/assets (all CC0). Freesound: https://freesound.org (filter licence = Creative Commons 0). Pixabay: https://pixabay.com/sound-effects/ (Pixabay licence, free).

## HDRI (download)

`public/assets/textures/sky.hdr`: Poly Haven, CC0, 2K is enough: "venice_sunset" (literally Venice at golden hour), or "kloppenheim_06" / "spruit_sunrise" as alternatives. https://polyhaven.com/hdris

## Textures to generate (ChatGPT or Gemini image generation)

Save as PNG, 1024x1024 unless stated, in `public/assets/textures/`. Ask for **seamless / tileable** where marked; check the tile by placing two copies side by side. Normal maps are better generated from the albedo with a tool (for example https://cpetry.github.io/NormalMap-Online/) than asked from an image model.

| File | Prompt (paste as is) |
|---|---|
| `plaster-ochre.png` (tileable) | "Seamless tileable texture of weathered Venetian plaster wall, warm ochre colour, flaking paint, faint salt stains, flat even lighting, no shadows, no objects, photographic, top-down orthographic, 1024x1024" |
| `plaster-terracotta.png`, `plaster-rose.png`, `plaster-cream.png` (tileable) | same prompt with "terracotta red", "dusty rose pink", "pale cream" |
| `stone-istrian.png` (tileable) | "Seamless tileable texture of white Istrian limestone blocks with thin mortar joints, slightly worn, flat lighting, orthographic, 1024x1024" |
| `algae-band.png` (tileable horizontally) | "Seamless horizontally tileable strip texture of a canal waterline on a stone wall: dark green algae and black moss fading upward into pale stone, flat lighting, 1024x256" |
| `water-normal-1.png`, `water-normal-2.png` (tileable) | generate an albedo first: "Seamless tileable texture of calm canal water surface with small ripples, top-down, neutral grey, flat lighting, 1024x1024"; then convert to a normal map with the tool above (strength 2 to 3).
